articles.summary: Bwin te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Levante y Betis en Ciutat de Valencia correspondiente a la jornada 3 de LaLiga EA Sports 26-27
articles.body: Levante y Betis se enfrentan en el Ciutat de Valencia en la tercera jornada de LaLiga EA Sports 2026-27. El conjunto granota llega a esta cita después de empatar frente a Osasuna y sumar únicamente un punto de los seis posibles en sus dos primeras jornadas. El Betis, por su parte, ha arrancado bastante entonado: viene de imponerse al Valencia y completar un pleno de seis puntos en este inicio de campeonato. Favorito para el partido entre Levante y Betis El Betis parte como favorito para hacerse con los tres puntos... aunque el historial entre ambos equipos presenta una gran igualdad, con cinco victorias verdiblancas, cuatro triunfos del Levante y un empate en los diez últimos enfrentamientos. El conjunto andaluz tratará de mantener su pleno de victorias ante un rival que todavía no ha conseguido marcar en Liga. Las casas de apuestas reflejan el favoritismo visitante con una cuota de 2.20 en Bwin por la victoria del Betis, mientras que el triunfo del Levante cotiza a 3.20 y el empate a 3.40. Ambos equipos marcan El Levante todavía no ha conseguido marcar en sus dos primeros partidos de la temporada. Una circunstancia que contrasta con el inicio del Betis, que ha visto portería en ambas jornadas y además ha mantenido su portería a cero. Sin embargo, los antecedentes directos presentan una tendencia claramente favorable a los goles en ambas porterías, ya que esto sucedió en cuatro de los cinco últimos enfrentamientos entre ambos conjuntos. Con estos datos, las apuestas deportivas conceden una ligera ventaja al escenario en el que los dos equipos consiguen marcar. Bwin ofrece una cuota de 1.70 para que ambos marquen y de 2.00 para que al menos uno de los dos se quede sin anotar. Primer equipo en marcar El Levante comenzó perdiendo en uno de sus dos primeros compromisos ligueros, mientras que el Betis ha conseguido adelantarse en el marcador en sus dos partidos y ha convertido ese buen inicio en un pleno de seis puntos. Además, el conjunto verdiblanco comenzó ganando en tres de los cinco últimos enfrentamientos directos contra el Levante. Una tendencia que refuerza su favoritismo en este mercado. Bwin paga una cuota de 1.78 a que el Betis marcará primero, 2.20 a que lo hará el Levante y 10.00 a que el encuentro finalizará sin goles. Número total de goles (Over/Under) Los dos equipos han protagonizado hasta ahora partidos de pocos goles, ya que en ninguno de sus dos primeros compromisos de la temporada se superaron los 2.5 tantos totales. Los antecedentes directos, sin embargo, ofrecen una perspectiva diferente: en cuatro de los cinco últimos duelos entre Levante y Betis se alcanzó esa cifra. El potencial ofensivo del conjunto verdiblanco puede contribuir a elevar el ritmo goleador de un encuentro en el que el Levante necesita mejorar sus registros en ataque. Bwin ofrece una cuota de 1.88 para que se marquen más de 2.5 goles totales y de 1.82 para que no se alcance esa cifra.

articles.title: El Girona no engaña a nadie
articles.standfirst: Para Casino Gran Madrid sigue siendo el gran favorito a ganar la Segunda División, a pesar de sus dos tropiezos
articles.summary: Para Casino Gran Madrid sigue siendo el gran favorito a ganar la Segunda División, a pesar de sus dos tropiezos
articles.body: El arranque de la Segunda División ha dejado una paradoja que merece explicación. El Girona, sin ganar todavía en sus dos primeras jornadas, sigue siendo el máximo favorito de las casas de apuestas para hacerse con el título de la categoría. El conjunto de Montilivi empató 1-1 en casa ante el Leganés, logrando el empate en el último minuto tras ir por detrás en el marcador, y después cayó por 2-1 en su visita al Córdoba. Pese a ese balance de un punto de seis posibles, Casino Gran Madrid mantiene al Girona como principal candidato al ascenso directo, a cuota 6, un respaldo que se explica por la calidad de su plantilla, muy superior sobre el papel a la del resto de la categoría, y por la confianza en que el bache inicial se corrija en cuanto el equipo coja ritmo de competición. El primer perseguidor es el Almería, a cuota 7. El conjunto andaluz, habitual en las quinielas de ascenso de las últimas temporadas, tampoco ha empezado con buen pie. Ganó en la primera jornada, pero cayó 1-0 en su visita al Tenerife el fin de semana pasado. Comparte esa misma cuota el Mallorca, que baja a la categoría de plata tras su descenso de Primera con un proyecto de la máxima ambición, aunque su último resultado tampoco fue el esperado tras caer 2-0 en su visita al Granada. Un peldaño por debajo en Casino Gran Madrid, a cuota 8, aparecen Las Palmas y el Real Oviedo. El conjunto canario es, de hecho, el único de los grandes favoritos que ha arrancado con dos victorias. Se impuso 2-0 en su visita al Ceuta, y logró vencer al Albacete en casa en el último minuto. El Oviedo, en cambio, solo ha podido sumar un punto, ante el Granada. El Eibar aparece bastante más alejado, a cuota 15. Cierran la lista de los principales candidatos, ya a cuota 19, Castellón y Granada. El conjunto castellonense firmó un discreto empate sin goles ante el Sabadell en su último partido, mientras que el Granada, paradójicamente, es de los pocos equipos de este grupo que sí sumó de tres al imponerse 2-0 al Mallorca. Lo que deja claro este reparto de cuotas es que, en un mercado a largo plazo como el de campeón de liga, dos jornadas apenas alteran la jerarquía marcada por el potencial de las plantillas. El Girona sigue siendo, para Casino Gran Madrid, el equipo llamado a pelear por el ascenso directo pese a su irregular inicio, mientras que casos como el de Las Palmas o el Granada, pese a sumar puntos con más solvencia, todavía no han conseguido moverle el sitio a un favorito que, de momento, solo convence sobre el papel.

articles.title: 'Playgrounds are more important than Playstations': PM Narendra Modi's message to India's youth
articles.summary: More sports News: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday stressed the importance of sports in building a healthy society and encouraged youngsters to choos.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday stressed the importance of sports in building a healthy society and encouraged youngsters to choose “playgrounds over Playstations”. Speaking to athletes during the Khelo India Dialogue via video conferencing, the Prime Minister said sports should become a part of everyday life rather than being seen only as a co-curricular activity in schools.Sports should become a way of lifePM Modi said it was encouraging to see sports finding a place in the daily timetable of youngsters along with studies. He said a strong sporting culture would develop when schools and families started treating sports as an important part of life."When time table is being made for career and studies, sports is also getting its place. This is the change due to which India's trust in its sporting future is increasing. Sports culture is established when schools do not consider sports periods as a co-curricular activity, but as a way of life. This is how the talent pool is developed, and the children get support from their families. Sports centers are more important than screens. Playgrounds are more important than Playstations. It will only happen when our youth will take this approach forward," he said.The Prime Minister also spoke about the value of sportsmanship beyond the playing field. He said sports can help create a healthy society, improve family life and build a better work culture."We often hear that, for a healthy society, a good family system, and a better work culture, the sportsman spirit is essential. And this spirit is very difficult to learn without going to the sports field. Sports not only teach us to become champions, but sports also teaches us to become better competitors. Rising, falling... falling and then rising again... Sports brings this zeal within us," he said.'Those who play, they blossom'PM Modi said success in sports is not limited to winning medals or matches. According to him, an athlete's success also brings pride to their family, school, district and state, while also increasing the country's prestige."It signifies the blossoming of the individual and the family, as well as enhancing the nation's pride. When an athlete succeeds, that success is not theirs alone; it elevates the identity of their family, boosts the prestige of their school and college, and strengthens the recognition of their district and state. The world begins to identify that city or state by the athlete's name," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Why is Alex Nylander joining Calgary Flames after finding limited NHL opportunities with Toronto Maple Leafs
articles.summary: NHL News: Alex Nylander joins the Calgary Flames on a professional tryout after struggling to secure his position in the NHL with the Toronto Maple Leafs. Discover how his strong AHL performance could lead to a vital career reboot in Calgary.
articles.body: After two seasons with the Toronto Maple Leafs organization, Alex Nylander is heading to the Calgary Flames on a professional tryout at training camp. The move gives the 28-year-old forward another shot at fighting for an NHL roster spot after limited action at the highest level in Toronto.This follows Nylander having one of his better recent seasons in the AHL with the Toronto Marlies. He played a part in helping the Marlies to a Calder Cup win, but his NHL opportunities remained scarce.Why did Alex Nylander join Calgary Flames now?The pro tryout provides Alex Nylander another chance to vie for NHL employment, and it also means he’s in the Calgary Flames’ training-camp plans.Nylander had 24 goals, 29 assists and 53 points in 65 regular-season games with the Toronto Marlies in the 2025-26 AHL season. He scored six goals and added seven points in 24 playoff games as Toronto claimed the Calder Cup.That outing is why Nylander remains an intriguing depth option even with an inconsistent NHL career. The Buffalo Sabres selected him eighth overall in the 2016 NHL Draft, but he has recorded 49 points in 126 NHL games.Nylander most recently played in the NHL in 2024-25 with the Toronto Maple Leafs, where he appeared in five games and did not record a point. Most of his recent production has been at the AHL level, though.His move to Calgary is thus a chance to reboot his NHL career. But there’s no guarantee of an NHL contract or a spot on the roster with the PTO. Nylander will have to impress the Calgary Flames in training camp and preseason.Could Calgary Flames become Alex Nylander’s NHL breakthrough?The Calgary Flames offer Nylander a new environment, though a permanent NHL spot is still up for grabs. His strong AHL production makes a strong case for another opportunity, while his career NHL numbers explain why the Flames will likely be cautious with him.Nylander’s immediate goal is simple: take his scoring success with the Toronto Marlies and parlay it into an NHL opportunity with the Calgary Flames. Alex Nylander is exiting the Toronto Maple Leafs organization after two seasons, signing a professional tryout with the Calgary Flames, and the 28-year-old forward is coming off a solid 2025-26 AHL season with the Toronto Marlies, helping them win the Calder Cup. Nylander could get another chance to play in the NHL in Calgary.The move gives Nylander a fresh opportunity after limited NHL action in Toronto. He recorded 24 goals and 53 points in 65 AHL games last season before adding seven points during the Marlies’ championship run. His NHL experience includes stops with several teams, making Calgary another important chance to revive his career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Super League: Wigan Warriors beat depleted Hull KR 46-0 to return to top of table after Sir Billy Boston tributes
articles.summary: On an emotional night at the Brick Community Stadium following the death of the legendary Sir Billy Boston at the age of 92, Wigan return to the top of the Super League table ahead of Leeds' match on Friday with a big win over a weakened Hull KR side; tributes to Boston ahead of the match
articles.body:
Boston, who was made rugby league's first knight last year, died on Tuesday morning , four days after the funeral of his wife Lady Joan.

An emotional pre-match tribute saw Boston's son Stephen carry a Wigan shirt bearing his name onto the halfway line, where it was draped over the same throne upon which Boston had sat when the club celebrated his knighthood last July.

Two seats were left vacant in the directors' box in tribute to Boston and his wife, and the home team warmed up in black T-shirts emblazoned with his number two prior to an impeccably-observed minute's silence.

Once the action got under way, Matt Peet's men duly racked up a record-extending 13th consecutive Super League win that restored them to the top of the table ahead of Leeds' trip to St Helens on Friday.

Liam Marshall helped himself to a hat-trick, while Zach Eckersley - the latest recipient of the number two jersey that Boston made his own - scored twice in a nine-try show to which Adam Keighran contributed a try and 10 points with the boot.

Rovers head coach Willie Peters, battling injuries and suspensions, named a team featuring three club debutants with an eye on next week's home clash with Huddersfield.

The defending champions are in real danger of slumping out of the top six and while the commitment of their weakened side could not be questioned, they were miles away from posing any kind of threat to a home team clearly hungry to wrest back their title.

The visitors held out for 10 minutes with Bill Leyland making a fine try-saving tackle on Jai Field before Marshall crossed for the game's first converted try.

Field zoomed onto Harry Smith's clever kick to double Wigan's lead, then Smith again was the instigator with a perfectly delivered 40-20 kick to set up Eckersley's opener on the right flank.

The half-time damage could have been worse for Rovers, as both Smith and Marshall had further tries disallowed, before Marshall and Eckersley each scored their second amid a torrential downpour just before the break.

Keighran converted his own try after Eckersley tapped back a Smith kick 12 minute into the second half, but Rovers dug deep and enjoyed a sustained spell of pressure on the Rovers line, forcing a series of drop-outs and bulling close through Arthur Mourgue and Sam Luckley.

Just after the hour mark Rovers thought they had been rewarded for their efforts when one of their debutants, Frankie Dearlove, splashed over in the corner, but replays showed a Wigan arm had prevented the ball being grounded, and the try was chalked off.

Marshall completed his hat-trick by blazing down the left with 12 minutes on the clock, and Wardle also jinked over after fine work from Field as the hosts wrapped up victory in a manner that would have made their late, great hero proud.

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+ .

articles.title: Fantasy Football Fades: Here are the wide receivers our analysts are avoiding for the 2026 season
articles.summary: Our analysts go around the table and give you the one wide receiver they are staying away from in 2026 fantasy football drafts.
articles.body:
Wide receiver is easily the deepest position in fantasy football. Each season, we see plenty of wideouts emerge as sleepers deep in your draft, while similar players bust out. While there are more chances to land a top WR, you also have to be aware of the players to avoid. Yahoo analyst Matt Harmon, Hayden Winks, Joel Smyth, Justin Boone, Ray Garvin and Scott Pianowski share the one WR they're fading in drafts in 2026.

Beyond off-field and medical concerns for Rashee Rice, I'm not so sure his role is as secure as many project. One-hundred-and-twelve wide receivers have run 600 or more routes since 2023, and Rice's 4.69 air yards per target ranks 112th, with a decent gap to 111th in Greg Dortch at 5.23. With Kenneth Walker III in town to provide a real-deal rushing game, some of those underneath "extension of the run game targets" could disappear, especially around the goal line.

The Chiefs were a massively underwhelming offense last year while funneling so many short targets to Rice; they have every incentive to mix up their approach. — Matt Harmon

The early warning signs surrounding Evans on the 49ers are not optimistic. The 33-year-old wideout has been in and out of practices this summer due to a variety of lower-body soft tissue injuries — the kind that have plagued him for a while now. Evans has missed 12 games over the last two campaigns and has dealt with hamstring issues every year since 2019. The veteran is also coming off arguably his worst statistical season with career lows in several categories, including yards per target, yards after the catch per reception and catch rate.

The opportunity for significant fantasy production still remains in San Francisco's offense — especially with Evans' touchdown potential — it's just hard not to avoid questions about his age and durability. Meanwhile, the target competition could be tougher than originally thought, with De'Zhaun Stribling emerging, George Kittle expected back in the opening weeks and Deebo Samuel Sr. joining the mix, on top of Christian McCaffrey commanding his usual volume. Any week Evans is healthy he'll have top-24 upside, but the red flags make him a risky fantasy WR3. — Justin Boone

I compared Tate to DeAndre Hopkins, Calvin Ridley and Jeremy Maclin before the draft, as my ninth overall player . He's pretty polished for a 21-year-old early declare but his skill set isn't necessarily fantasy friendly. He mostly plays outside and runs routes on the vertical stem. His speed and tackle breaking is fine, not elite, so there's less incentive to make sure he has 2-3 easy receptions per game like others who have gone as high in the draft. That role for the Titans is going to go to slot Wan'Dale Robinson, whether we like it or not. Beyond that, there are real concerns with the Titans. It's the first year in a new scheme, one that we don't even love. The OL might be the worst in the NFL and Cam Ward stunk behind it last year. Tennessee was 30th in scoring and 30th in passing yards last year. The preseason games haven't eased my concerns with Ward's development. Tate has gone catchless on 25 routes in them. — Hayden Winks

Metcalf's perception has been far better than his fantasy production for years. We have to go back to 2020 (!!) to find a top-20 fantasy season for the Year 8 wideout. That top fantasy season came on the back of 40 Russell Wilson touchdowns in a dominant offense. I believe you're doing yourself a disservice by not drafting a player with more upside. In a year with Metcalf as the bonafide WR1, Aaron Rodgers targeted him under 100 times in his 15 games, with much more volume going to quick routes rather than Metcalf's vertically focused route tree. Now that Michael Pittman Jr. — a true WR2 who fits Rodgers play style very well — is joining the Steelers, are we expecting Metcalf to show out with his 42-year-old QB? — Joel Smyth

Alec Pierce was activated off the PUP list on Thursday, but that does absolutely nothing to change how I feel about him for fantasy football this season. If anything, the amount of time he has already missed makes me even more concerned.

Pierce is coming off a breakout year with 47 catches for 1,003 yards and six touchdowns despite limited volume, and Indianapolis rewarded him with a massive contract extension. With Michael Pittman Jr. gone and Josh Downs dealing with his own injuries, the opportunity should have me excited. Instead, Pierce has spent essentially the entire offseason and training camp out while recovering from ankle surgery. That is valuable preparation time lost for a receiver whose game is built around speed and explosive plays.

Now add Daniel Jones returning from an Achilles tear, and there are simply too many variables here for me. I would rather take shots on players like Courtland Sutton or Chris Godwin Jr. Pierce may ultimately be fine, but I don't want to draft into this much uncertainty. He's a full fade for me in 2026. — Ray Garvin

Rashee Rice is probably my No. 1 fade on the entire 2026 draft board, but it doesn't make sense for us to double up on picks. Just understand I agree with Matt on this one.

Instead, I'll pivot to Tyson, the New Orleans rookie. I understand the buzz tied to him, as people are excited about his Arizona State production and tape. Alas, Tyson is dealing with a hamstring injury – the same problem that dogged him in college – and he will be out to start the season. Normally that would turn any player, especially an unproven one, to an auto-fade, but the market continues to price Tyson as a quasi-priority pick.

I don't like drafting into injuries during the summer, because I know injuries will come looking for us no matter what we do. Heck, look around the August landscape. Despite teams limiting starters in exhibition games and exercising all the precautions during practice, we already have an injury-riddled landscape. To the managers who think they'll draft Tyson and safely stash him on an IR spot, I warn that those IR spots will surely have company before September is over.

Also remember the gap-week concept – most players off long-term injuries probably need one "prove-it" week before we can trust them in our lineups. That costs you another game. And even if everything goes perfectly with the Tyson rehab, the upside still might be capped — the Saints already have an alpha WR in Chris Olave and a catch-gobbling tight end in Juwan Johnson, and Tyler Shough is an average-at-best quarterback. I know Tyson can be a fun fantasy pick, but let's wait until 2027 before we draft him proactively. — Scott Pianowski

articles.title: Dolphins Reportedly Send WR Tutu Atwell Back To Rams For RB Jarquez Hunter
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins have reportedly traded wide receiver Tutu Atwell back to the Los Angeles Rams in exchange for running back Jarquez Hunter.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Rams are reuniting with a former wide receiver of theirs. Tutu Atwell is going back to the Rams as the Miami Dolphins have agreed to trade him for running back Jarquez Hunter, ESPN reported Thursday. Atwell returns to Los Angeles five months after leaving the franchise in free agency. Originally selected by the Rams in the second round of the 2021 NFL Draft out of Louisville, Atwell appeared in 64 games and hauled in five receiving touchdowns and ran in another over four seasons, operating as both a downfield threat and return specialist. Atwell was on the Rams Super Bowl LVI roster, but did not play the second half of the season due to a shoulder injury. Atwell signed a one-year contract with his hometown Dolphins in March, but now rejoins head coach Sean McVay’s offense ahead of the regular season. He joins a crowded receiver room including the likes of Davante Adams and Puka Nakua as options through the air for reigning NFL MVP Matthew Stafford. Hunter, a fourth-round draft choice by Los Angeles in 2025 out of Auburn, joins a Miami backfield seeking additional depth. During his rookie season in 2025, Hunter primarily contributed on special teams, appearing in five games. The Rams open the season against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia on Sept. 10. articles.title: PSG To Start Champions League Title Defense Against Barcelona, Man City
articles.summary: Two-time defending champion Paris Saint-Germain will host Manchester City and travel to Barcelona in the Champions League main phase this season.
articles.body: Two-time defending champion Paris Saint-Germain will host Manchester City and travel to Barcelona in the Champions League main phase this season, after the 36-team draw was made Thursday. PSG has won three straight visits to Barcelona — including a 2-1 win in the league phase last October — since imploding in the famous 6-1 loss in March 2017 that is known as the "Remontada" game. The French champion again plays Aston Villa, after a Super Cup win this month, and goes to Champions League newcomer Como, coached by Cesc Fabregas, in an eight-game slate that starts in two weeks' time. Real Madrid will host Inter Milan and make two trips to London, at Arsenal and against Shakhtar Donetsk. Ukraine’s champion is playing home games at Stamford Bridge, where Madrid's returning coach José Mourinho was beloved by Chelsea fans in a pair of title-winning spells there. Barcelona will host two English clubs — Man City and Europa League winner Villa — plus its former player Fabregas with Como. A long trip to Azerbaijan awaits to face debutant Sabah in Baku. Arsenal, the beaten finalist last year, will host Madrid, Borussia Dortmund and Sabah, and travel to Bayern Munich. Bayern got a second English opponent, with a trip to Manchester United, plus two Norwegian opponents, hosting Bodø/Glimt and visiting Viking. Bayern also will go to Atletico Madrid whose Metropolitano Stadium will host the final next May. Liverpool got trips to Inter Milan and Fenerbahce in what looked one of the more favorable slates of eight games. Atletico will again come to Anfield where Liverpool won 3-2 last September. Atletico also will play both Norwegian teams and is one of four teams heading inside the Arctic Circle to play on Bodø/Glimt ’s artificial turf. Dortmund, Lille and newcomer LASK also will travel to the remote fishing town, and one team must make the trip in January. Sabah also will host Dortmund, Napoli and Slavia Prague. Fans also have two long trips from Azerbaijan to England to face Arsenal and Man United. Como has a second trip to Spain, to play Real Betis as well as Barcelona, and will welcome PSG and Man United to its picture-postcard lakeside stadium home. Four Debutants In Champions League Draw Four newcomers will debut in this Champions League edition: Como from Italy, coached by Cesc Fabregas; LASK of Austria; Viking from Norway; and Azerbaijani champion Sabah, which was founded only in 2017. Sabah coach Valdas Dambrauskas is already making headlines for his curious origin story in soccer. The money he won as a young contestant on TV quiz show "Who Wants to be a Millionaire" in his native Lithuania funded a trip to study coaching in England. Another first this season is an African coach taking his team into the main phase. Former Manchester City and Barcelona star Yaya Touré guided Slovakian champion Slovan Bratislava through its qualifying playoff Wednesday. Slovan will visit PSG and host Inter Milan. Champions League Draw Details UEFA’s draw software allocated eight opponents to each team — four home games, four away — with two opponents taken from each seeding pot. Seeding was decided by ranking a team's European results over the past five years. Teams could not be paired with an opponent from their own country. The first round of games is played Sept. 8-10 with the first six rounds played through December. The league phase resumes in January with the eighth and final round on Jan. 27. The top eight teams in the final standings go direct to the round of 16 in March. Teams placed ninth to 24th enter the knockout playoffs in February to decide the other eight teams in the round of 16. Teams placed 25th to 36th are eliminated. The 36 teams will share prize money of about 2.5 billion euros ($2.9 billion) Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: FSU running back makes Earl Campbell Tyler Rose Watch List
articles.summary: Florida State running back Quintrevion Wisner has been named to the Earl Campbell Tyler Rose Award Watch List.
articles.body:
Florida State football running back Quintrevion Wisner is up for a big honor. He's landed on the Earl Campbell Tyler Rose Award watch list . It's given to the top offensive player who graduated from a high school or plays for a Texas-based Division 1 school. Wisner is also on the Doak Walker Award watch list .

Wisner went to DeSoto High School in DeSoto, Texas. He was a productive player as a senior with 846 rushing yards and six touchdowns; he also registered 35 receptions for 466 yards and four scores.

In college, Wisner has produced as well. In three seasons with the Texas Longhorns , he played in 38 games and amassed 1,734 rushing yards and nine touchdowns plus 66 receptions for 457 yards and two scores. He produced 597 yards rushing and three touchdowns and 146 receiving yards and one touchdown in 2025.

Wisner suffered a minor injury earlier this month. However, he will be available in the season opener against the New Mexico State Aggies, according to head coach Mike Norvell. He'll be in the rotation with Ousmane Kromah and Samuel Singleton Jr. this year.

He ran for over 1,000 yards in 2004. So, Wisner is more than capable of handling a sizeable workload if an unforeseen injury occurs or if he simply outplays Kromah or Singleton. Hopefully that's not the case, but it's good for FSU to have a guy that can do so if need be.

articles.title: Why WRC drivers expect Rally Paraguay to be “almost a second Safari”
articles.summary: Heavy rain, slippery red clay and a high puncture risk have crews predicting a rally of survival — and potentially a lottery — in Paraguay
articles.body:
WRC drivers expect Rally Paraguay to become something of a lottery, with forecast heavy rain threatening to create "almost a second Safari Rally" this season.

Paraguay surprised many crews as the gravel rally made its WRC debut last year with its distinctive red-clay gravel surface proving difficult to master. This year the rally is the longest of the WRC season at 358.88km, featuring five new stages.

In dry conditions, the road surface becomes increasingly polished with each passing car, making it extremely slippery. That effect is only magnified in the wet. Protecting tyres will also be crucial with bedrock coming up through the road surfaces in places.

However, the hot topic in the service park ahead of the event is the weather. Friday is expected to remain dry, but heavy rain is forecast for Saturday and Sunday.

"Someone said it can be almost like a second Kenya. If rain comes, it can be extremely difficult. It seems like tomorrow can still be more straightforward in the dry, which also here is quite demanding with many jumps and compressions. There can be a lot of punctures expected as well. It's not going to be too straightforward, especially if the rain kicks in," said Toyota's Sami Pajari, who took victory in Finland last time out.

According to Oliver Solberg , the level of rain that is due to arrive could be huge.

"It doesn't look like it's just a little bit of rain either. It looks like Niagara Falls. So I think when that comes, it will be much worse than Africa," Solberg told Motorsport.com.

"We have this red clay dirt and it's changing all the time. Realising where it's slippery is quite tricky already on shakedown. So I think when the rain comes, if the rain comes, it will be difficult everywhere. I like it. The more tricky it is, the better. The more things can happen, and the more things you can turn around."

Sebastien Ogier, Julien Ingrassia, Toyota Gazoo Racing WRT Toyota GR Yaris Rally1

Ready to fight for victory after his heavy crash at Rally Finland, reigning world champion Sébastien Ogier knows what it takes to tame Paraguay after winning the inaugural WRC version of the event last year.

However the Frenchman was frustrated to miss out on scoring the full 35 points after being caught in a late heavy rain shower. This year he feels the rally will pose even more of a lottery to crews.

"At least, in my point of view, this weekend will be a lottery. Tomorrow it's a puncture lottery, and after that it's going to be very complicated with the conditions, so you never know," Ogier told Motorsport.com.

"It's extremely challenging here. This clay road is basically giving no grip at all. So I think it's going to be very interesting. That's the word we always use in this condition when you don't know how to describe it, but it's going to be tricky."

In some aspects drivers believe it could be worse than Safari Rally Kenya given there are few open run-off areas in the stages to recover should off road moments occur.

Elfyn Evans, Scott Martin, Toyota Gazoo Racing WRT Toyota GR Yaris Rally1

"We had similar conditions here a little bit last year, maybe not as extreme as what we're going to face now," said Toyota's Elfyn Evans , who leads the championship by 30 points over Pajari.

"The thing is here, you actually have many more things to hit in a way than you do in Kenya. I know that sounds a bit strange saying there's nothing to hit in Kenya, but there's far less of this open grassland sections here and more of a proper road lined with trees and banks and rocks and all the rest of it. So that's going to be tough."

"The stages are fully dry basically at the moment. Some bits you can see already that the risk of cutting up and risk of puncture is already quite high. How they evolve with the amount of rain this forecast is going to be almost impossible to judge. I think we kind of have to try and deal with the best we can on the day."

Fourmaux expects fight to go to final Power Stage

Adrien Fourmaux, Hyundai World Rally Team Hyundai i20 N Rally1

Hyundai's Adrien Fourmaux impressed at this event last year having led the event on Friday before suffering a puncture. The Frenchman was then caught out by the rain as his i20 N ingested water.

Fourmaux believes he has the pace to fight for what would be a maiden WRC win but believes the rally may not be decided until the final Power Stage.

"I'm happy to come here. I know it's a tough one. I think we kept the lead for a long time last year, and then we lost it for a puncture, but then we kept second and then the last stage happened. But then there were few things before with the engine, drinking water, many things happened here, and I think it will happen again. But we've learned from last year," said Fourmaux.

"There are a lot of new stages. The rain is coming. It's going to be slippery. So I would say everything is possible until the last kilometre of the Power Stage.

"The roads are so compact on the dry. So when there is water, we are aquaplaning on top of it. It is like ice."

M-Sport prepares snorkels for heavy Paraguay rain

Jon Armstrong, Shane Byrne, M-Sport Ford World Rally Team Ford Puma Rally1

M-Sport-Ford is prepared for the worst having brought snorkels that can be attached to its Ford Puma Rally1 cars should standing water become an issue.

The impending weather could however provide a chance to the British team to capitalise on the tricky conditions.

"I think we could have a good result, but we know that we need everything to go to plan, and it hasn't been happening so far," said Rally Paraguay debutant Jon Armstrong.

"The only thing I can say it's similar to is the Goodwood Rally stage, which also has these shiny places when it starts to get more and more polished off from the cars driving over it. Only it seems here, it doesn't take so many cars for it to start to polish."

"I think it's probably the slippiest gravel you'll ever get. And with the amount of rain they're saying there's going to be on Sunday, maybe a boat will be better. Let's see," added Armstrong's team-mate Josh McErlean.

articles.title: Welbeck scores on debut as Chelsea beat Luton in Carabao Cup
articles.summary: Chelsea progressed to the third round of the Carabao Cup with a comfortable 2-0 victory over League One side Luton Town at Stamford Bridge.Xabi Alonso named...
articles.body:
Chelsea progressed to the third round of the Carabao Cup with a comfortable 2-0 victory over League One side Luton Town at Stamford Bridge.

Xabi Alonso named a strong starting XI, with Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers both featuring as Chelsea looked to maintain their unbeaten start under their new manager. However, Luton arrived in confident mood, having gone 15 matches without defeat in all competitions, and frustrated the hosts during a goalless first half.

The hosts gradually increased the pressure, with Rogers striking the crossbar late in the opening period and Estêvão also going close.

The breakthrough arrived five minutes after the restart when Malo Gusto delivered an inviting cross into the box and Danny Welbeck rose above the Luton defence to head home on his Chelsea debut.

Chelsea eventually found their second in the 70th minute. Estêvão drove into the box and sent a dangerous low delivery across goal, with Luton defender Hakeem Odoffin unable to prevent the ball from deflecting into his own net.

The visitors offered little threat in response as Chelsea controlled the closing stages. Jamie Gittens struck the post in stoppage time, while João Pedro was also denied from close range, but two goals were enough to send the Blues through.

Chelsea will face Leeds United in the third round.

articles.title: 'Disappointed' Bannigan steps down as Monaghan boss
articles.summary: Gabriel Bannigan steps down from his role as Monaghan manager after two years at the helm.
articles.body:
Gabriel Bannigan said he was "disappointed" to be stepping down from his role as Monaghan manager after two years at the helm but said the "goalposts have been moved" and he could not continue.

Bannigan initially joined Monaghan as part of Vinny Corey's management team in 2022 before succeeding Corey as boss in 2024.

Under Bannigan, Monaghan won the Division Two title in 2025 and reached successive All-Ireland quarter-finals where they were knocked out by Donegal and then Louth.

The Farney men were relegated from Division One this year after a tough league campaign in which they failed to pick up a point.

They bounced back well in the Ulster SFC with wins over Cavan and Derry but suffered an extra-time defeat against Armagh in the decider.

"I ma very disappointed to announce that I am stepping down as manager of the Monaghan senior football team," Bannigan said in a statement.

"When I was appointed two years ago, I accepted the challenge of leading the Monaghan team through an inevitable period of transition and it has been an absolute privilege to do so.

"I have always been 100% honest with the Monaghan people since I was given the honour of managing our senior footballers, I did not want to walk away from this project that I have put so much into.

"Over the last number of weeks, I worked hard on my plans for 2027 to build on the excellent foundations now in place. During this period, I have come to realise that the goalposts have moved, and the conditions are not right for me to continue and therefore I believe a new management team and fresh voices are now required to take Monaghan football forward."
authors: Lauren McCann - BBC Sport NI Journalist

articles.title: Paige Bueckers Among New Unrivaled Contracts Announced, Joins Olivia Miles, Flau'Jae, More
articles.summary: A handful of new players have been announced for the Unrivaled Season 3 roster.
articles.body:
A handful of new players have been announced for the Unrivaled Season 3 roster.

The league announced Thursday that Dallas Wings star Paige Beuckers will return on a multi-year deal. She joins Olivia Miles, Flau'Jae Johnson and a handful of other notable names.

Along with Bueckers, the league announced that Natasha Cloud, Courtney Williams, Chelsea Gray, Marina Mabrey, Shakira Austin and Dearica Hamby will be a part of next year's season of Unrivaled.

The second season of Unrivaled was another success as Nepheesa Collier won the one-on-one tournament and Rose BC won the championship. Rose BC featured Shakira Austin, Lexie Hull, Sug Sutton, Angel Reese, Kahleah Copper and Gray, who won Finals MVP.

Collier took home the regular season MVP, and Reese won Defensive Player of the Year.

Earlier this week, Unrivaled announced that it had raised money that puts its valuation at $650 million, a testament to the success it has had since its debut in 2025.

The league, which Breanna Stewart and Collier co-founded, gives players an equity stake in addition to their salaries, and the players are the largest shareholder group heading into the new season. The value of the player-equity pool is up to nearly $200 million.

While Unrivaled will not add any new teams this season, it will expand the competition window. Season 3 begins on Jan. 8.

Unrivaled gives fans the chance to watch their favorite WNBA stars compete in a different way, pitting three against three rather than traditional five-on-five. The one-on-one tournament also adds a unique element to the league.

Season 3 figures to be a star-studded year as well, with Bueckers and more of the league's premier players already on board.

articles.title: Crystal Palace vs Man City: Premier League – prediction, teams, lineups
articles.summary: Manchester City travels to Crystal Palace, looking to build on their late show in their opening Premier League match.
articles.body:
Who: Crystal Palace vs Manchester City What: English football’s Premier League Where: Selhurst Park in London, United Kingdom When: Friday August 28, at 8pm local time (19:00 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 16:00 GMT ahead of our live text commentary stream.

Manchester City continue life after Pep Guardiola as they visit Crystal Palace in the second round of English Premier League matches.

Enzo Maresca has endured a mixed start to replacing the Spaniard as City manager, having lost 3-0 to Arsenal in the Community Shield before needing two late goals to turn their league opener against Bournemouth.

Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at the match, which is a rerun of the 2025 FA Cup final that saw Palace claim a famous win.

Maresca calls for reinforcements for Man City

City manager Maresca wants the club to spend the final few days of the summer transfer window finding “one or two more captains” to add to the squad for its push for trophies this season.

City’s summer clearout has seen lots of experienced players leave the club, including John Stones, Bernardo Silva, Rodri and Nathan Ake.

The two major signings have been young midfielders in 18-year-old Ayyoub Bouaddi and 23-year-old Elliot Anderson , and City is aiming to bring more players in before the deadline late Tuesday.

Maresca wants whoever is signed to immediately be part of the leadership group in City’s increasingly young squad.

“We have experienced players for sure. We have leaders,” Maresca said at a news conference Thursday ahead of a Premier League match at Crystal Palace on Friday.

“Now we need to wait four or five more days to see if we can add one or two more captains to Ruben (Dias) and Erling (Haaland) who are the captains.”

Reports in the UK media say City retains an interest in Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez, who Maresca appointed as vice captain during their time together at the London club.

Maresca insisted City was not close to making further signings at this stage.

“No, no, no,” he said. “The one that arrived is Ayyoub (on Wednesday) and then we will see in the next four or five days.”

City did see one further big-name departure on Thursday when Tottenham Hotspur signed ‌Omar Marmoush from a season-long loan, ⁠with the deal including an obligation to make the Egypt forward’s move permanent at the end of the season.

Bouaddi needs time at Man City despite big fee

Bouaddi is “ready to go” for his City debut at Crystal Palace on Friday, but Maresca called for patience with the most expensive teenager in Premier League history.

A star of Morocco’s run to the World Cup quarter-finals, Bouaddi joined City on Wednesday for an initial 100 million euros (£85.6 million, $117m) from Lille.

City moved for Bouaddi after selling a trio of midfielders in Spain’s World Cup-winning captain Rodri, Tijjani Reijnders and Nico Gonzalez in recent weeks.

“We will see how long it is in terms of adaptation but for sure he is ready to go,” Maresca told his pre-match press conference on Thursday.

“He doesn’t look 18 – he looks older which is important but in this case we need to go slowly because he is young, came from a different country.

“No rush for him. For sure he will help us now and in the future. But he is just 18,” he said.

“It is my job and it’s the club’s job to manage him in the best way, don’t put pressure on him, he is young and he needs time.”

How have Crystal Palace started the new Premier League season?

Palace lost their opening match of the season 2-0 at Everton.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Thierno Barry scored the goals as the Eagles came unstuck at the Toffees.

Palace had started the game as the better side, and edged the possession throughout, although Everton ended with five shots on target to the away side’s four.

What happened the last time Palace played Man City?

Man City beat Palace 3-0 at Etihad Stadium in a Premier League clash in May.

Antoine Semenyo and Omar Marmoush netted first half goals, while Savio sealed matters with six minutes to play.

What happened in the corresponding game between Palace at Man City last season?

Man City were also 3-0 winners at Selhurst Park in the corresponding fixture last season.

Erling Haaland netted a brace while Phil Foden chipped in with the second on the day.

When did Crystal Palace last beat Man City?

Palace beat City 1-0 in the FA Cup final in May 2025.

Eberechi Eze scored the only goal after 16 minutes of the match at Wembley Stadium in London.

When did Palace last beat Man City in the Premier League?

Palace last beat City with a 2-0 in the Premier League in October 2021.

Wilfried Zaha and Conor Gallagher scored either side of Aymeric Laporte’s first half sending off.

When did Palace last record a home win against Man City?

Palace won 2-1 against City at Selhurst Park in the Premier League in April 2014.

Glenn Murray and Jason Puncheon handed Palace a two-goal lead before Yaya Toure netted in the 78th minute to set up a tense finish.

The Opta supercomputer has given City a 57.5 percent chance of victory and Palace a 20 percent chance.

This will be the 76th meeting between the sides with City winning 41 of the matches, and Palace emerging victorious on 18 occasions.

Ismaila Sarr is still recovering from a groin injury so misses out for Palace, as doesChadi Riad due to a knee injury.

articles.title: Praggnanandhaa scripts history, becomes first Indian to win Grand Chess Tour
articles.summary: Chess News: Indian Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa produced a remarkable turnaround against Fabiano Caruana to win the Grand Chess Tour Finals and secure the biggest.
articles.body: Indian Grandmaster R Praggnanandhaa produced a remarkable turnaround against Fabiano Caruana to win the Grand Chess Tour Finals and secure the biggest title of his career in St. Louis on Thursday (local time).Praggnanandhaa overturned a six-point deficit at the start of the day, winning both rapid games against Caruana before holding his nerve in the blitz section to seal a 15-13 victory.The triumph also saw Praggnanandhaa create history. He became the first Indian player to win the Grand Chess Tour.The victory earned the young grandmaster the $200,000 first prize.Praggnanandhaa erases six-point deficitCaruana entered the final day with a commanding six-point advantage after the classical games. Praggnanandhaa, however, came out firing in the rapid section and won both games to completely change the complexion of the contest.With the momentum firmly on his side, the Indian needed to navigate the four-game blitz phase without surrendering his lead.The opening blitz encounter nearly went against Praggnanandhaa. He had winning chances but blundered during a time scramble, allowing his position to deteriorate. Caruana could not find the winning continuation, and the game eventually ended in a draw.Praggnanandhaa then managed to keep the match level in blitz and completed his comeback with a 15-13 aggregate victory.Caruana had taken early controlThe final had initially looked heavily tilted in Caruana's favour.Praggnanandhaa lost the first classical game 6-0, leaving himself with a significant deficit heading into the remainder of the contest.He responded in the second classical game by holding Caruana to a 3-3 draw. Although the result meant Caruana still carried a six-point advantage into the final day, Praggnanandhaa's comeback in the rapid games changed everything.Wesley So finishes thirdGM Wesley So also produced an impressive comeback in the third-place match against GM Vincent Keymer.The two players split the rapid games, trading victories before So took complete control in blitz.So won all four blitz games to clinch the match with one game still remaining, sealing an 18-12 victory over Keymer.Praggnanandhaa's victory, meanwhile, marked a landmark moment for Indian chess as he became the country's first Grand Chess Tour champion.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Harsh Singh once struggled to put food on the table with his family; five years later, he became India’s first male judoka to win Commonwealth Games gold
articles.summary: More sports News: The road to sporting success is rarely easy. For some athletes, the biggest battles begin long before they step onto the mat. Judoka Harsh Singh's jou.
articles.body: The road to sporting success is rarely easy. For some athletes, the biggest battles begin long before they step onto the mat. Judoka Harsh Singh's journey is one such story.Before making history at the Commonwealth Games by becoming the first Indian male judoka to win a gold medal in the men's 60kg category, the 23-year-old from Dwarka, Delhi, had seen his family go through some of its toughest days.There were times when the family struggled to arrange even one proper meal. During the COVID-19 lockdown, his father, an electrician, was left without a steady source of income.Harsh watched his family struggle, but refused to let the circumstances break him. He continued to train, holding on to one dream - to make a name for himself in judo and build a better life for his family.A young boy with a big dreamHarsh's introduction to judo came when his family could not afford many luxuries. His father travelled from one house to another, repairing electrical switches, plugs and appliances. He earned around Rs 500 to Rs 1,000 a day, which was the family's main source of income.For Harsh, pursuing sport brought additional expenses. There were training costs, competitions, travel and the need to maintain a proper diet. Every tournament required money, even as his family struggled to manage their daily needs.Still, Harsh kept training.The toughest yearsThe COVID-19 pandemic made life even harder. With the country under lockdown, Harsh's father could no longer travel from house to house for electrical work. The income stopped and the family's savings began to disappear.The situation became so difficult that the family sometimes struggled to arrange meals. They eventually had to borrow money to keep the household running.Even during those difficult days, Harsh refused to quit judo. He continued to train and carried his family's hopes every time he stepped onto the mat.2024 changes everythingAfter years of struggle, Harsh's fortunes began to change in 2024. He won gold at the National Championships, giving his career a major boost.The success also opened a new door. Harsh earned a job with the Indo-Tibetan Border Police. articles.title: Nebraska Finishes Strong to Claim the Spikes Under the Lights Title at AT&T Stadium
articles.summary: The Huskers adjusted to the unusual surroundings to sweep Florida and SMU and earn $150,000 prize
articles.body:
Under the bright lights of AT&T Stadium, Nebraska opened a bit slow but saved its best for the final act.

The top-ranked Huskers eked out a 21-19, 21-17 victory over No. 17 Florida and then dominated No. 11 SMU in the final (21-12, 21-11) to win the Spikes Under the Lights exhibition event Thursday night in Arlington, Texas.

With the title, the Huskers earned an extra $150,000 for the program on top of the $200,000 that the four participating teams received.

"Of course there is money on the line, but it meant a lot more than money," NU coach Dani Busboom Kelly said. "It was a fun way to end a long day."

After the final point, the NU players celebrated with an oversized novelty check before waving to the crowd of an estimated 40,000 fans at the home of the Dallas Cowboys.

The regular season gets underway Saturday evening for the Huskers against UNLV in Las Vegas. NU then faces No. 2 Texas on Sunday afternoon at T-Mobile Arena.

Here are takeaways from the pair of matches:

The event might have felt like a home match, with most of the fans filling AT&T Stadium wearing red and cheering for the Huskers.

However, NU struggled to adjust to their surroundings. The evening featured lots of Nebraska fans cheering in a fast-paced event. The sets were only played to 21, with each team getting one timeout.

"It's definitely a different environment. Everything's very fast-paced," NU senior middle blocker Andi said. "There's a lot happening at once. All the lights, all the fans. But it's an awesome environment, and it was a super fun game."

Jackson said it took them a little bit to settle into the environment of the large football stadium. The teams practiced on the court Thursday morning, but the lights were positioned lower for the matches, which made it challenging for setters and passers to pick up the ball.

She said the magnitude of the event hit her and her teammates during the serve-and-pass practice.

"Everyone's jaws were just on the floor. You couldn't even believe that we get to play in this venue, and it's so massive, and it's so cool, and the lights are everywhere," she said. "We've heard about it, and we've seen it on social media, but actually being here now, it's very surreal."

After a sluggish first match against Florida, the Huskers sat around for an hour while SMU and Penn State were playing, and Julia Cole performed several songs.

The layoff didn't appear to have any impact as Nebraska came out on fire against SMU. The Huskers jumped out to a 12-2 lead in the first set and were hitting .455 with six kills on 11 swings. Meanwhile, the Mustangs were scuffling with just one kill on 11 attacks and four errors.

The second set started closer, but NU turned an 8-7 advantage into an 18-9 lead before NU coach Dani Busboom Kelly emptied the bench.

The Huskers hit .339 for the match, with nine players recording a kill.

Florida led in both sets before the Huskers closed strong.

The Gators were up 19-18 in the first set before NU scored the final three points on a service error and two Manaia Ogbechie kills.

"Being an underclassman and stepping up and doing that with the little experience that she has in those high-pressure moments is so impressive that I'm proud of her," Jackson said about Ogbechie. "It really shows that she's really earned the right to be there, and she's earned that spot. In practice, I see what she can do, so I'm really excited for you guys to see everything that she can do."

In the second set, Florida was up 13-10 before the Huskers scored five points in a row. The Gators closed to 19-18 before Virginia Adriano notched a kill and Teraya Sigler ended it with an ace.

Busboom Kelly said in a postgame radio interview that she gave her team a B- grade for the performance.

Jackson said they stopped having fun during the match while they were struggling and got a little tense. During a challenge, they reminded each other to have more fun on the court and enjoy the experience.

"It sounds cheesy, but truly, when you're uptight, it's really hard to play good volleyball and trust your training," she said in an interview on TNT. "We went out there, and I looked at (Adriano), and I said, 'Hey, let's see a smile.' Little things like that, having fun, smiling, cheering – it really helps you feel loose and play your best volleyball. We know what we've trained for, and we know that we can trust our training. You saw in those last moments it was super smooth, super clean volleyball, and we just trusted each other and trusted our training."

If NU wants to improve in any area, it's getting more kills from its outside hitters. Over the two matches, Sigler led NU with 13 kills and six errors on 33 swings. Harper Murray hit negative in the first match but rebounded for eight kills and six errors on 28 attacks.

The duo struggled to put away in-system attacks at times and finished with a combined kill percentage of 41.2 percent.

All 16 players saw the court during the two matches. Campbell Flynn and Jayden Robinson got in during a double substitution against Florida while everyone else saw action versus SMU.

Most of the bench players made the most of their short time on the court. Skyler Pierce recorded three kills on four swings while Kenna Cogill, Keoni Williams and Ryan Hunter all notched a kill on their only attack.

Whitney Lauenstein looked impressive in her debut for Penn State. The Waverly graduate spent her first two years with the Huskers before sitting out a year and transferring to Texas. After two seasons with the Longhorns, she was granted a medical hardship for an additional year of eligibility and elected to play for the Nittany Lions.

After mainly playing opposite for most of her career, Lauenstein started at outside hitter for PSU. She finished with 12 kills, the highest total of anyone in the three matches, while hitting .450. She added three digs and a block.

It wasn't enough to power the Nittany Lions to a win as they fell 24-22, 21-18 to SMU.

articles.title: Thursday Football: South Fort Myers rallies to stun Riverdale
articles.summary: South Fort Myers scored twice in the final three minutes on Jaydon Henderson touchdown passes to defeat Riverdale 20-17.
articles.body:
South Fort Myers mounted a furious comeback with two touchdowns in the final three minutes to upset Riverdale 20-17, handing the Raiders their first loss at home in two years on Thursday night.

Trailing 17-6 in the fourth quarter, it appeared grim for the Wolfpack after a fumbled snap at the Riverdale goal line led to a turnover.

With three minutes left in the game, South Fort Myers junior quarterback Jaydon Henderson threw a 34-yard bomb to sophomore Tenaris Kearse for a touchdown to bring the Wolfpack within a score.

The South defense came up with a sack fumble, recovered by junior Ty Fletcher, to give the team a chance to take a lead with less than two minutes to go.

It took Henderson just two throws – a 20-yard strike to sophomore Jer'Shard Benjamin before he went back to the well, finding Benjamin over the middle for a 14-yard score to for the lead.

"We kept telling the kids at halftime, especially on defense, just keep playing, keep playing," South Fort Myers head coach Matt Holderfield said. "We knew the defense was going to have to make some plays, and I thought the defense made some good plays there and kind of forced the situation a little bit.

"Jer'Shard just made some great plays, Tenaris made some great plays there. (Henderson) threw some good balls, let them block a little bit and we got something done at the end."

Defense dictated the contest early, and the Raiders got on the board first after Henderson fumbled a snap and Riverdale senior Ky'moni Gordon scooped it up and ran 30 yards for a touchdown.

South answered in the second quarter when Henderson uncorked a ball for a 33-yard touchdown to Aiden Boyd on fourth down.

The Raiders gained some separation before halftime with a 10-yard rushing touchdown by junior Josiah Bataille and a safety on a South punt to make it 17-6 at halftime.

The tide began to turn in the fourth quarter when mistakes starting piling up for the Raiders, who had been playing a clean ball game until then.

South senior Devontae Humphries blocked a punt at the beginning of the fourth quarter to set up the Wolfpack with a chance to score.

However, South could not cash in after a goal line fumble, recovered by Riverdale senior Kaleb McIntyre.

The Wolfpack defense never let up, continuing to give their offense chances. And once Henderson and his receivers got going, they were met with little resistance.

After Benjamin's go-ahead touchdown, he sealed the game on defense with an interception of junior quarterback Terrance Taylor.

"We got to play four quarters," Riverdale head coach Kendoll Gibson said. "We let that one slip in the last three minutes. It was tough. We kind of got away from what we were doing all night. We held Jaydon in check, and we kind of let him get in a rhythm the last four, five plays. We got to play four quarters. They're too athletic not to finish."

Chemistry in the trenches paid off in the final minutes. The offensive line gave Henderson time to make plays, while the defense came up with a clutch strip sack with two players sandwiching Riverdale junior quarterback Rayful Guest for a key turnover in the final two minutes.

"The good thing about our o-line and d-line is those guys have been together and they know each other and they know how to play with each other, and it definitely shows because they play hard together and they got a lot of experience there," Holderfield said. "It's just continuing to get better at what we're doing."

The Wolfpack could be without a couple important players next week. Boyd, a former Riverdale player, was ejected for a second unsportsmanlike penalty after his touchdown. Then, in the game's final minutes, senior defensive lineman Ja'Dell Carter was assessed a second unsportsmanlike, leading to his ejection. The FHSAA will decide if the ejections should be upheld, which would lead to suspensions for both players in the team's game against Gulf Coast next Thursday.

"We can't do stupid things to hurt ourselves," Holderfield said. "They got to understand if we're going to be a playoff team and go deep in the playoffs, you got to be able to remove that emotion out of it and just play football."

Don't call the Wolfpack road warriors just yet. South went 4-2 on the road last season, including a fourth quarter comeback against Naples similar to the one on Thursday night.

Despite the 2-0 road record to start the season, Holderfield believes his squad has room to grow before hailing them as a team that travels well.

With seven road games this season, South will have plenty of chances to prove it.

"We've got to earn a couple more things like this before I can say that it's us doing it, but I think we can get there," he said.

The defense held South's explosive offense in check for nearly the whole game. The Raiders limited the run game of Henderson, who only had two rushing attempts go for more than 10 yards. And several of South's biggest plays didn't come until the final three minutes.

"We let Jaydon get into a rhythm throwing the ball – something that we didn't do all night," Gibson said. "Our d-line was kind of gassed. We put them on the field back-to-back-to-back almost. We didn't blitz and were kind of sitting back, and, if we don't put pressure on Jaydon, he can find something."

The Raiders erred after the Wolfpack made it a one score game. The team called two pass plays when they got the ball back, which eventually led to the pivotal sack fumble.

"Terrible decision from my end," Gibson said. "Probably should've just ran the ball."

The key to regrouping will be getting back to Riverdale football. The Raiders' schedule starts with seven playoff teams from last year, and the team will go on the road to play Bishop Verot next week.

"We're going to play our style," Gibson said. "We trust what we do. It sucks. I told our boys we should feel upset. We literally gave the game away in my eyes. I felt like we played the better game the entire game, but when you don't finish four quarters, that's what happens."

The Rams are required to reduce their roster to 53 players, meaning several players who spent the offseason competing for a job will soon be looking for their next opportunity. articles.title: Rams Winners & Losers: Ty Simpson secures backup status?
articles.summary: Ty Simpson may just have beaten out Stetson Bennett to serve as Matthew Stafford’s backup
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams put the finishing touches on an unbeaten preseason led mostly by strong quarterback play. They held onto a last-minute surge by the Los Angeles Chargers to maintain a 20-18 lead.

Sunday brings an important deadline in the NFL calendar. All 32 teams must soon cut to their initial 53-man regular season rosters. The "Winners & Losers" list is largely shaped by those who helped build their case, although the framework is mostly set by those who sat out of Thursday night's finale.

Who performed well on an individual level against the other LA team? Which players are watching their stock fall?

Ty Simpson came into Thursday night's game with the lowest average depth of target (ADOT) among all rookie quarterbacks —by far. Simpson averaged 4.80 air yards in the first two preseason games. That mark improved to 6.1 yards against the Chargers. That would still rank last among all first-year signal callers.

Simpson completed 18 of 23 passes (78%) for 119 yards and an impressive touchdown throw on the run. He finishes the preseason 47 of 60 (78%) for 382 yards, three scores, zero turnovers, and a passer rating of 109.9.

This isn't meant to bash Simpson. Many fans didn't like the pick. He's won a lot of people over. There are still a number of questions that remain unanswered. We are able to check some boxes: short and intermediate area accuracy, value-add mobility, ability to throw on the run, sack avoidance, and an overall poised composure. We haven't seen Simpson throw deep and it's fair to wonder whether his efficiency can be sustained when the offense requires him to be consistently more aggressive.

I think fans are losing sight of the fact that Simpson seems to be a high floor player. We haven't seen the rookie make many mistakes. We still have no idea how high his ceiling is. The preseason really taught us nothing in that regard.

So big picture, Simpson made as convincing as a case to be Stafford's backup as to be reasonably expected. That is a win for the Rams. In terms of his potential to takeover the starting job as soon as 2027 and his viability as a franchise quarterback? That is still completely unknown.

The difficult truth is that the Rams may be completely set at running back with Kyren Williams, Blake Corum, and Ronnie Rivers. Sean McVay is adamant that he trusts Rivers and values his contributions on special teams.

With Jarquez Hunter getting traded to the Miami Dolphins in exchange for Tutu Atwell just hours before kickoff, there was an opportunity for Dean Connors and Jordan Waters to make their final argument to make the team. Connors did everything he could to help his case. It still may not be enough.

Connors rushed 18 times for 69 yards (3.8 average, although several carries came late to milk the clock and not put emergency QB Simpson in harm's way). He also added three catches for 24 yards and a score through the air. This was his third touchdown of the preseason. It also happened to be quarterback Matthew Caldwell's first NFL touchdown.

And if the Rams end up cutting Connors, he may draw attention from other teams. Running back tends to be a position where there is a short learning curve to adapt to a specific scheme. They are largely plug and play. That makes them somewhat interchangeable.

With their wealth of riches in the backfield, that may be enough for the Rams to not keep Connors on the 53-man roster. If there isn't a stark drop off from Connors to Waters, why not bet that one of them will be available for the practice squad. It's not personal. It's a numbers game.

You can't ask any more from your kicker than being perfect in the preseason. Harrison Mevis made all six of his attempts across the three exhibition games. He hasn't been asked to kick from distance—his longest attempt was from 40 yards out. Still, you can only convert the opportunities you get. This is real and positive momentum heading into the regular season.

With another five catches on six targets for 42 yards, Daniels was clearly LA's most talented and productive preseason receiver. The Rams were intent on running the passing game through him when they could, especially in last week's contest against the New Orleans Saints.

But on-field production isn't Daniels' biggest challenge. He's clearly behind Jordan Whittington and Konata Mumpfield on the depth chart. If he makes the roster, it may be a long while before we see the rookie again.

Bailey played only two snaps on defense. He started the game and then exited after Justin Herbert's fumble on the second play. Did the Rams want to limit Bailey's time in order to keep him healthy because he's in line to make the roster? The only other alternative is that Bailey was injured during the game. There were no such reports. This is a noteworthy result worth monitoring ahead of Sunday's cutdown to the 53-man roster.

Norton is someone who has consistently flashed on preseason tape over the last two years. He has a high motor and can often be seen chasing ball carriers downfield. It's impressive for a big man. Teams that need additional depth along the defense interior should have Norton atop their target list as the NFL trims their rosters. He can help someone and approaches the game in the right way.

Stetson Bennett obviously didn't play on Thursday night. He filled up the box score last Saturday, though he was erratic as a passer .

Simpson seems ready to backup Matthew Stafford. If the rookie ends up winning the job, I fail to understand why it is worth keeping Bennett around. Would it be nice to have someone who knows the offense as an option if something happens to Stafford? Sure, but there will be veteran options like Jimmy Garoppolo available and somehow losing Stafford and Simpson would mean the Rams have awfully bad luck.

Bennett had to win the backup job convincingly. He didn't. For that reason there is not sound logic behind potentially keeping him around.

Justin Herbert's night was cut short after he threw a 64-yard pass to split two Rams defenders for a touchdown. Lampkin was on the wrong side of that deep ball. He also played late into the game despite having one of the most hyped starts to training camp. It's not how you start, it's about how you finish. Lampkin's last impression likely won't help him in what should be a lean cornerback room.

Failed to make a reception on four targets, and when quarterbacks looked his way he was often blanketed. Simpson gave him a contested catch opportunity deep along the left sideline and the corner handily won the rep.

articles.title: Sean McVay sheds light on Rams' trade for Tutu Atwell
articles.summary: Sean McVay told reporters that the Tutu Atwell trade is not related to a potential suspension for Puka Nacua.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams made a trade out of nowhere on Thursday afternoon, just hours before their preseason game against the Los Angeles Chargers. They traded running back Jarquez Hunter to the Miami Dolphins for Tutu Atwell, reuniting with the receiver they just let walk in free agency five months ago.

It was a surprising trade for both teams, especially given the depth Los Angeles already had at wide receiver. Immediately, some fans questioned whether this deal was in preparation for a possible Puka Nacua suspension.

Sean McVay says that isn't the case. He told reporters after Thursday's game that acquiring Atwell had nothing to do with any possible suspension for Nacua. He says the Rams just wanted more depth at the position.

Additionally, Atwell won't bump any wide receivers that were previously going to make the team off the roster. That's an indication the Rams could keep as many as seven wideouts.

Atwell spent the last five years with the Rams after being a second-round pick in 2021 out of Louisville, but he never lived up to expectations. Even after signing a $10 million fully guaranteed contract last offseason, he barely played any snaps for the Rams.

The Dolphins signed him to a modest $1.4 million deal this offseason, with the Rams now responsible for $1.2 million of that sum. It's a low-risk deal for Los Angeles, especially if Hunter wasn't expected to make the team anyway.
