articles.title: Astros finished off series win over Yankees. Three players had contributions that stood out
articles.summary: Christian Walker, AJ Blubaugh and Jeremy Peña came through in key spots to help Houston leave the Bronx with a series win and some momentum amid a chaotic we...
articles.body:
NEW YORK - With a clean all-around showing, the Houston Astros claimed a series at Yankee Stadium on Thursday. Four pitchers combined to allow five hits. Their lineup scratched out three runs against Gerrit Cole and two more against relievers. After a horrid homestand and a front-office shakeup , they took two of three against the Yankees and maintained a one-game division lead.

No city knows better the importance of a full cast, but here were three key players in a 5-1 win Thursday :

Walker entered Thursday in a 6-for-50 funk, with one home run in August. The first baseman said that he worked on a swing adjustment pregame to free up his hands.

"The feel the last few days hasn't been there," Walker said. "I felt stuck, like it was hard to get inside of sinkers. So pregame today just tried to get out of my own way and get free, just set up the machine and let the hands work, try not to get too clunky, keep my body out of the way."

Cole is no hitter's idea of a favorable matchup. The right-hander wields one of the sport's best fastballs, averaging 96.8 mph and holding hitters to a .185 average against it entering Thursday. Still, Walker said, that left him little choice but to rely on his reactions.

"Not a lot of time to think and work through mechanics," Walker said. "Just trust what I'm seeing, try to be on time and find the barrel."

In his first at-bat, Cole led with a 96.6 mph fastball. Walker shot it to right field for a single at 107.5 mph off the bat. In his second, Walker rolled over a slider for a ground out. He came up again in the sixth.

The Astros clung to a 1-0 lead at that point. Cole had worked his first five innings on 54 pitches. He got two outs in the sixth before Daulton Varsho staged a pivotal plate appearance. Cole got ahead 0-2 on Varsho, who worked a seven-pitch walk to extend the inning. Houston manager Joe Espada deemed it "the at-bat of the game." Walker agreed.

It brought up Walker, who took a fastball for ball one, then saw a curveball in the zone. Cole began the day throwing his curveball just 10.9% of the time to right-handed hitters this season, but he did so 34% of the time to Astros righties in this outing. Walker sent the pitch 369 feet to right-center field, where it just cleared the wall.

"That one was a reaction," Walker said. "I hit the first fastball (in the first at-bat) the other way. Second at-bat, he went with different shapes.

"He doesn't stray away from his fastball - it's one of the best in the game. I knew it was coming again, a matter of time. But just tried to stay in the moment and trust what I was feeling. That curveball just popped out of his hand, I saw it early and luckily I put a good swing on it."

Statcast deemed his 24th home run of the season a homer in one of 30 major-league ballparks. Here, it proved the game's decisive swing.

For an embattled Astros bullpen , Blubaugh has been invaluable as a multi-innings option. No pitcher in the majors had logged more relief innings than Blubaugh this season entering Thursday. Across his last 45 appearances, the right-hander had a 2.38 ERA.

Blubaugh's ability to cover multiple innings is one reason he has rarely appeared late in games in high-leverage situations. His outing Thursday presented a case for why that could change down the stretch.

The Astros took a 4-1 lead into the bottom of the seventh inning. Left-hander Steven Okert recorded three outs in the sixth, allowing some loud contact. Lefty Bennett Sousa had allowed four runs in a decisive seventh inning Wednesday . The Yankees lineup featured seven left-handed hitters Thursday.

Blubaugh began the day holding left-handed hitters to a .179 average and a .585 OPS. He entered the seventh inning to face the bottom three spots in New York's order. Jazz Chisholm Jr. swung through a 97.8 mph fastball for a strikeout. Austin Wells whiffed at a 97.2 mph fastball for another.

José Caballero lined a single, but Blubaugh induced a pop-up from leadoff hitter Trent Grisham . Bryan Abreu warmed during the top of the eighth. But after the Astros added a run, Blubaugh returned for a second inning of work, with the 2-3-4 spots in the Yankees order due up.

"I think definitely the situation, the atmosphere, how the game went, how the series was sitting, I think that all had a little influence on how it went tonight," Blubaugh said. "But it was a lot of fun, for sure."

Blubaugh retired the side in order in the eighth. He struck out Luis García Jr., who was 7-for-12 with five RBIs in the series' first two games, chasing a 3-2 changeup. He touched 98.8 mph to Cody Bellinger , who lined out on a full-count fastball. All six hitters Blubaugh retired were left-handed.

"He was throwing that first-pitch pitch strike, off-speed pitches, setting up a good fastball all the way up to 99 (mph)," Espada said. "That was pretty impressive. We're looking for guys that can pitch some leverage innings, and I think he's showed that he can do that."

Blubaugh made his 51st outing of the season. He entered just seven of the previous 50 in the seventh or later with the Astros tied or leading by four or fewer runs.

"I wouldn't say I have a preference on what part of the game," Blubaugh said. "Honestly I just like having the ball in my hands. Whatever gets the 'W' at the end of the game, that's all I'm really looking for."

Peña missed two games on the last homestand after being hit on the right hand by a 100 mph pitch. It was not a comfortable sight for Houston, then, when the shortstop took a 96 mph fastball from Cole to his left hand in his second plate appearance.

Peña was checked by a trainer but remained in the game. His speed immediately came into play. Two batters later, Isaac Paredes fought an 0-2 fastball into the right-field corner. Peña, who was moving on the pitch, scored from first base for the game's first run.

Cole exited after six innings. Yerry De Los Santos drew the seventh for the Yankees. The right-hander entered holding right-handed batters to a .194 average against his sinker this season. No righty had homered against the pitch in 42 plate appearances.

In a 1-1 count, De Los Santos bore a 95.1 sinker over the inside corner. Peña turned on it, his compact swing producing a 382-foot home run to left field.

It was Peña's second home run of the series. He had one in his prior 16 games, a stretch over which he hit .138. Houston's offensive dip in that span dovetailed with the struggles of its sparkplug. Few things feel more crucial to its playoff hopes than a resurgence from Peña over the season's final month.

"We're getting there," Peña said Thursday night. "I feel like there's definitely stuff I've learned and I can use it as a plus. It's 30 games left and it's time to finish strong."

Peña went for X-rays on his left hand after the game, which "came back clean," he said. It was a positive punctuation for the Astros to a series in which they needed to perform.

"It's huge," Peña said. "Every game means so much to us, and we played great baseball here."

AJ Blubaugh showed why more high-leverage work could be in his future after shutting down the Yankees for two innings Thursday. (Jonathan Pensiero/MLB Photos via Getty Images)

Jeremy Peña contributed with his legs and bat Thursday, scoring from first on Isaac Paredes' single for the Astros' first run and later hitting a solo homer. (Jonathan Pensiero/MLB Photos via Getty Images)

articles.title: Chargers fall to Rams in final preseason game: Recap of LA's loss
articles.summary: The Chargers closed out preseason play with a loss to the Rams. Read our full breakdown to see how the game played out.
articles.body:
The Chargers closed out the preseason with a 20-18 loss to crosstown rivals Rams at SoFi Stadium.

Quarterback DJ Uiagalelei was sacked and fumbled past midfield with under a minute, cutting short a potential game-winning drive. The turnover allowed the Rams to milk the clock and walk away with the narrow victory.

RB Greg Desrosieres Jr: 8 carries, 110 yards (13.8 YPC), TD

WR Quentin Johnston: Reception, 65 yards, TD

Head coach Jim Harbaugh gave quarterback Justin Herbert more run this week. Herbert fumbled on his second snap of the opening drive, but completely redeemed the unit on the next series by uncorking an explosive 65-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Quentin Johnston

Quarterbacks Trey Lance and DJ Uiagalelei traded reps as they battled for the primary backup position. Lance didn't complete a pass on two attempts but chipped in with 22 rushing yards. Uiagalelei was the more productive out of the two after entering late in the first half, finishing with 11-of-18 passing for 141 yards.

The Chargers' ground attack found immense success behind running back Gregory Desrosiers, who averaged an incredible 13.1 yards per carry to lead a rushing unit that compiled 204 total yards.

After allowing 146 rushing yards last week, the Chargers' defense was more stout in this department as they allowed an average of 3.8 yards a carry on the night.

Kicker Cameron Dicker missed a crucial opportunity just before halftime, as his 49-yard field goal attempt sailed wide right, leaving the Chargers empty-handed heading into the locker room. Dicker missed a kick in each of the three preseason games.

Punter JK Scott had a rough go, struggling with hang time. Scott's first punt only went for 20 yards. This comes weeks after failing to make an attempt to tackle a 49ers return man that resulted in a touchdown.

Injury troubles hit the wide receiver corps as Dalevon Campbell went down with a non-contact injury during a route in the third quarter and had to be helped directly to the locker room. Campbell was among the team's summer standouts.

The Chargers will finalize their 53-man regular-season roster over the weekend before shifting their focus toward the regular-season opener against the Cardinals.

articles.title: Rangers announce £8.5m deal for Girona winger Kim Min-su on four-year contract
articles.summary: Rangers have announced the signing of winger Kim Min-su from Spanish club Girona.The 20-year-old joins the Scottish Premiership giants on a four-year deal wi...
articles.body:
The 20-year-old joins the Scottish Premiership giants on a four-year deal with an option for another year after his £8.5 million release clause was triggered.

Minsu was born in Korea but moved to Catalonia with his family aged ten, and has lived there since.

He joined Girona's youth ranks as a 16-year-old in 2022, and made his senior debut two years later.

He made seven senior appearances for the club, including one in the Champions League, in 2024-25.

The South Korean winger spent the 2025-26 season on loan at FC Andorra, where he bagged six goals and four assists in 40 games in La Liga 2.

He played twice for Girona in the competition this season before completing his move to Rangers.

The left winger becomes the Gers' 12th signing of the summer They had tried to re-sign Mikey Moore on loan from Tottenham Hotspur after his successful spell last season.

They also pulled the plug on a deal for Couhaib Driouech due to an issue flagged during his medical.

Min-su met manager Derek McInnes before their Europa Conference League play-off game against Jablonec, but was not in the squad.

He will likely make his debut when they face Aberdeen in the league this weekend.

The South Korean forward has shown significant quality throughout his career, and will be expected to hit the ground running in Scotland.

He has the technical tools to be a success in Scotland, and could potentially be a huge hit for his new club.

They will now look to potentially conclude their summer business with the signing of Kevin Kelsy .

articles.title: Fleetwood in contention as Lee leads Tour Championship
articles.summary: Defending champion Tommy Fleetwood shoots a four-under 66 to put himself in contention at the Tour Championship at East Lake in Atlanta.
articles.body:
8 MW Lee (Aus); -6 V Hovland (Nor), C Morikawa (US), C Gotterup (US); -5 R Gerard (US), A Bhatia (US), L Aberg (Swe), S Scheffler (US)

Selected others: -4 T Fleetwood (Eng), M Fitzpatrick (Eng), R Fox (NZ); -3 R MacIntyre (Sco), W Clark (US); -2 J Rose (Eng), A Fitzpatrick (Eng), R McIlroy (NI)

Defending champion Tommy Fleetwood shot a four-under 66 to put himself in contention, four strokes off first-round leader Min Woo Lee at the Tour Championship in Atlanta.

However, Northern Ireland's Rory McIlroy endured a mixed start in his bid to win a record-extending fourth Fedex Cup, bogeying two of the first four holes before fighting back on the back nine to sign for a 68.

Lee carded a bogey-free 62 to set the pace at eight under as he equalled his best round on the PGA Tour in its season-ending event at East Lake.

Australia's Lee is two strokes clear of Norway's Viktor Hovland, who triumphed in 2023, and American duo Collin Morikawa and Chris Gotterup.

It was a fine display from Lee, who was second from last in the BMW Championship a week ago and found himself without a partner for most of the day, with JJ Spaun withdrawing through injury after four holes.

"It was a little strange at first, just like looking for a playing partner and you're just there by yourself," said Lee.

"It was more just maintaining speeds and not rushing because I would just catch the group in front and wait. So I had to just slow down a little bit. It worked out."

Ominously, world number one Scottie Scheffler ended his round with a birdie on the 18th to sit at five under, with England's Matt Fitzpatrick in the mix at four under after also making a birdie four on the concluding hole.

Scotland's Robert MacIntyre is at three under, with the highlight of his day arriving on the sixth hole when he rolled in a putt from over 30 feet for an eagle.

England's Justin Rose and Alex Fitzpatrick both signed for rounds of 68 on a day when none of the 29 players in the field to complete the round went over par.

The winner on Sunday will take home the Fedex Cup and a $10m (£7.4m) prize.

There will be live text coverage of the final round on the BBC Sport website and app from 18:00 BST.

articles.title: Josh Sweat trade rumors: NFL insider quashes rumors
articles.summary: Could the Cardinals trade Josh Sweat?
articles.body:
The future of Arizona Cardinals linebacker Josh Sweat has been discussed a lot this offseason. Trade rumors came up this week with the Cardinals in Green Bay for a joint practice and their preseason finale, and it happened to be the week that Sweat finally came off the PUP list. There is a connection with Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon, who was the Cardinals' head coach when Sweat signed with them.

While rumors swirl, the message remains consistent from the team and from national outlets.

ESPN's Adam Schefter was on ESPN Milwaukee and said what has been said before.

"I try to deal in facts and realities, and all I can tell you is I know there have been teams that have reached out to them (the Cardinals), and I know they have been told they're not trading him. Now, could they change their stance down the line? Sure, but there have been teams that recently have reached out and they have told those teams, 'We are not trading him.'"

Sweat led the Cardinals with 12 sacks in 2025 and is really their only known pass-rushing threat.

He did not participate in the voluntary offseason program. He did not practice during minicamp. He started training camp on PUP with a knee issue that head coach Mike LaFleur said was more maintenance than anything, but it took a month before he was activated.

General manager Monti Ossenfort has said that they aren't trading Sweat.

Now, after this weekend, we will see if anything changes.

articles.title: Giants still standing show their mettle taking down D'backs in 6-1 win
articles.summary: The San Francisco Giants have lost many of their frontline players, but Thursday's win over Arizona, powered by Drew Gilbert, Landen Roupp and others showed...
articles.body:
Rebounding after rough losses hasn't been a strong suit for the San Francisco Giants . Thursday, though, against one of the team's top 2026 tormentors, it all came together.

A night after blowing a six-run lead in the largest ninth-inning collapse in franchise history, San Francisco protected a one-run lead into the later innings (before adding four more in the eighth) and getting good work from the bullpen in a 6-1 victory over the Diamondbacks.

"Some sort of karma or baseball gods or whatever involved," manager Tony Vitello said. "If you're just talking about the circumstances from (Wednesday) and what we've struggled with this year with bouncing back appropriately, the team we played today is an excellent team and they've played more confident than we have when we've matched up - you wrap it all into one, and it stacks up."

Thursday's victory had a little bit of everything. Drew Gilbert hit a leadoff homer, Christian Koss blazed from first to third on a sacrifice bunt and scored on Gilbert's sac fly, Landen Roupp snapped his five-game losing streak and the bullpen chipped in with four scoreless innings after Wednesday's disaster to help the Giants improve to 2-8 against Arizona.

"It was a great answer for a tough inning (Wednesday)," said rookie reliever Trent Harris, who worked two scoreless innings. "But you know there's a lot of unspoken words. Nobody really had to say anything. We knew what happened and we just came out ready to play today."

Given the collapse against the Reds the previous day, the biggest at-bat of the night might have come from Jung Hoo Lee. Lee hadn't started two games in a row because of a bruised right elbow, but he pinch hit in the eighth and drew a 10-pitch walk, getting the sellout crowd going along with the rest of the lineup.

LOB: Arizona 7, San Francisco 4. 2B: Eldridge (16). HR: Moreno (11), off Roupp; Gilbert (8), off Cabrera. RBIs: Moreno (66), Gilbert 2 (36), Eldridge (36), Cox (7), Hill (4), Whitcomb (8). SB: Perdomo (18), Cox (5). CS: Moreno (2). SF: Gilbert. S: Furman, Whitcomb.

Runners left in scoring position: Arizona 4 (Vargas, Fernandez, Waldschmidt 2); San Francisco 3 (Whitcomb, Cavanaugh 2). RISP: Arizona 1 for 8; San Francisco 3 for 8.

Inherited runners-scored: Clarke 1-1, Burgos 2-1. HBP: Cabrera (Koss).

ABS Challenge: Cabrera (Ball-Confirmed); Perdomo (Strike-Overturned to Ball).

Umpires: Home, Alex MacKay; First, Alan Porter; Second, Jim Wolf; Third, Roberto Ortiz.

"As soon as he walked to the plate, I think (the fans) added a little energy to the whole thing," Vitello said. "The fact he battled the way he did and got on base, the guys in the dugout even at this level turn into cheerleaders when you put together an at-bat like that and you're spoiling a bunch of pitches. When you put everything into a little box, it was kind of like dynamite for us to start the inning."

After a single by Rafael Devers, Lee scored on Bryce Eldridge's double; rookie outfielders Jonah Cox and Turner Hill provided RBI singles that inning, while third baseman Shay Whitcomb sent Cox in with a safety-squeeze bunt.

"We haven't really done that all year, come back from a tough loss and really show the grit that we still have," Koss said. "Drew sparking that right away in the first inning kind of helps, but we knew as a team that we needed to really bring it today, and we kind of saw it throughout the game."

With Willy Adames likely out for the rest of the season with an elbow injury, Koss has started 27 of the past 28 games and has a plus-2 outs above average (OAA), an advanced Statcast metric. Adames, who has played through back issues this season, had a minus-17, tied for worst in the majors.

The Giants have Marcelo Mayer, acquired from Boston at the deadline, waiting in the wings. When he's ready to come off the injured list - he expects to be out of a walking boot for a bruised foot soon - Koss is likely to shift back to third, where he has also played well.

Gilbert has gotten onto a tear and he's looking comfortable in the leadoff spot, going 11-for-27 with three homers in eight games. Gilbert has also improved defensively after a bit of a slow start; he's now at a plus-3 OAA and his arm and range are both in the top 20%.

Roupp, now the team's No. 2 starter, has had his wobbles, but Thursday, he allowed only one run, a homer by catcher Gabriel Moreno, who clouted a changeup on the ninth pitch of his at-bat in the fourth. Roupp went five innings but he walked only two batters after he'd walked 19 over his previous five starts and had a 6.20 ERA in that stretch.

The focus for him Thursday was to pitch in the zone, particularly after some mechanical changes to keep his weight back and keep himself from flying open. "I figured some small things out," he said. "Tonight feels like a step forward."

Maybe, too, for the Giants as a whole, responding to one of the worst losses in team history with contributions from everywhere in a well-played game.

"That was rough," Roupp said. "It's never how you want to end a game, obviously, and it was just a good all-around game tonight. … We've just got to keep playing like that."

images.caption: Drew Gilbert (0) rounds the bases after hitting a solo home run off Jose Cabrera (53) in the first inning as the San Francisco Giants played the Arizona Diamondbacks at Oracle Park in San Francisco on Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026. (Carlos Avila Gonzalez/S.F. Chronicle)

articles.title: 5 takeaways from Rams' preseason win vs. Chargers
articles.summary: Dean Connors' final impression was a good one, while Ty Simpson capped off the preseason with another strong outing.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams went undefeated in the preseason, with a 20-18 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers sealing up their work. As the team moves toward roster cut-down day and the regular season, here are five takeaways from their final preseason contest.

With Jarquez Hunter off to Miami, there's a vacancy at the team's RB4 spot. That could be either a roster or practice squad spot, and it looks like Connors has it. He had another strong performance as a receiving back, while being the team's most efficient runner.

Connors also hauled in his third touchdown of the preseason, setting up this season to serve as a development year, and 2027 as a potential breakout season.

Simpson was excellent, efficient, and protective of the football, committing zero turnovers during his action across three games. He made proper reads, smart throws, and played within the structure of the offense. There are a lot of things the Rams can do with Simpson, especially with his mobility.

The team could not ask Simpson to be better. He has a long way to go in his development, but this preseason was the foundation he needs to build off of. He went 18-for-23 for 119 yards and one touchdown on Thursday.

CJ Daniels is an unfortunate cut candidate

After the Rams added back Tutu Atwell, receivers on the bubble could be in danger of losing a crucial roster spot. Considering the team will likely keep five tight ends on their first 53-man roster, they also already have Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Jordan Whittington, Xavier Smith, Konata Mumpfield, and now Atwell as receivers.

On top of that, Daniels had a good day with five catches for 42 yards, but he didn't have a dominant showing against the Chargers to perhaps change his status. Brennan Presley had another strong game, hauling in a touchdown pass from Simpson . The team likely values Daniels' upside, giving him the edge over Presley, but for the active roster, where does Daniels fit?

The special teams issues might continue into 2026

The Rams did a lot to fix their issues of 2025, but a new problem is starting to come to the surface, alluding to the overall concerns of the unit still lingering. Last season, it was the kicking game. This year, it could be the team's most consistent specialist, as Ethan Evans had a 24-yard shank against the Chargers.

Typically, I would ignore the miss, because Evans was excellent in preseason before that punt. Plus, he nailed a game-winning punt, pinning the Chargers at their own 1-yard line, so he still has that excellence in him. The problem is that I saw the inconsistency arise during joint practice with the New Orleans Saints. In an ideal world, this is a blip on the radar, but the Rams have lost the benefit of the doubt when it comes to their special teams unit.

It isn't sound-the-alarm time, but it might be good to know the alarm still works – just in case. The good news is that Evans' work typically speaks for itself. Let's hope it continues to do so, like his last punt of the preseason.

The Rams will have a strong practice squad

Regardless of who the team adds to their practice squad, the Rams will have a plethora of talent to call up if they need. Connors, Presley, Mario Williams, Elias Neal, Bill Murray, Daryl Peterson III (who strip-sacked DJ Uiagalelei to win the game), Mark Redman, and others should be able to slip onto the game-day roster without issue.

There will be plenty of call-up candidates throughout the season.

articles.title: Have expensively assembled Rangers improved at all under McInnes?
articles.summary: After crashing out of the Conference League, questions are mounting for Derek McInnes at Rangers, writes Tom English.
articles.body:
Where do you start? How do you catalogue the insipidness of Derek McInnes' Rangers team in Jablonec?

How do you catalogue the Pedro-Caixinha-in-the-bushes level embarrassment that the club experienced in their exit from European football on Thursday?

In Jablonec, Rangers were unspeakably awful, devoid of any cohesion, desire, threat, their manager reduced to saying how embarrassed and mortified he was multiple times post-match.

They had one shot on target the whole night, one goal scored in 210 minutes. Rangers fans in the stadium gave it to them with both barrels at the end.

McInnes apologised. The whole scene was cringe-making. He tried to explain what he was trying to do with his multiple switches of formation and attempted to explain why his side were "miles off it".

Talk is cheap in his position. There's a limited shelf life for that kind of thing at Ibrox.

The chat from some Rangers folk in the preamble was that the Conference League meant little to them, that an exit wouldn't spark an uprising, that no midweek European football could give them a chance to hurl themselves at the Premiership instead. Fine in theory, but not in reality.

The notion that a defeat would be met with a collective shrug by Rangers fans was never a serious proposition. This defeat sparked untrammelled fury.

McInnes would be as well staying away from social media. Winning in the bear pit of Pittodrie on Sunday is strongly advised.

What are Rangers? What is their identity?

Rangers were so flat in the Czech Republic, meandering about like confused men, showing weakness in the tackle and not a scintilla of wit. McInnes changed the shape of his four or five times and the poverty of their play didn't improve one iota.

"I look at us now and I'm thinking, well, we're no' great as a possession-based team at the minute," said McInnes in explaining his constant switches.

"We're not a counter-attacking team enough, or effectively enough, at times. We don't look like a team who are happy when we go direct. And teams need to be something."

Quite. And what are Rangers? What's their identity? What are they good at? In what areas are they improving?

McInnes was appointed in June, had a full pre-season, had six games and then a week off to prepare for the trip to Jablonec, only for Rangers to produce their worst effort of this, and many other, seasons.

During the dog days of his reign at Rangers, Russell Martin was once asked if he could name one or two things that were better on his watch - and he couldn't do it.

If McInnes was asked the same question now then there's no guarantee that he would come up with an answer, or at least, an answer that rang true.

Nobody really knows what his Rangers are, least of all McInnes, you suspect. He made three substitutions at the break on Thursday, a trio that brought his total of half-time replacements to 11 in seven games.

That betrays a manager who has either got his team wrong in the first place, hasn't been able to impart his message to his starters or doesn't have a dressing room capable of taking in what he's saying to them. Whatever the truth of it, it's not good.

He knows what he wants because he watched it on television the night before. Hearts had four new players in their starting line-up against Rapid Vienna and used another two off the bench.

Wouter Vrancken, in quick time, moulded them together and made something terrific out of them in winning their own Conference League tie in Austria.

McInnes praised his old club for the resilience of their players and the stomach they showed for the fight. The inference being that his own boys had little or none of that. Again you ask, why not?

Vast periods of this play-off went by without Rangers stringing more than four and five passes together. They pressed in ones and two or not at all.

They came across as a team that had just met, a collection of guys rounded up in a pub and coached by a character who had no idea what to do with them.

Where was Raskin? And why not sign experience?

Ibrox is a confused place right now. McInnes said his team looked young and inexperienced against Jablonec. This was on the back of announcing the signing of a 20-year-old winger and - if things go to plan - a 22-year-old striker.

If they need gnarled operators then why not sign some?

There was no Nico Raskin, the midfielder left at home, not because there'd been a bid for him, said McInnes, but because there might be.

If there were was a decent offer and the possibility of higher ones, his absence would have been understandable. If there was no bid then why was there no Raskin?

He was missed, said McInnes. A player who performed well at the World Cup and he's left at home? Odd.

McInnes said that his coaching staff are "elite in everything we do" in preparing the players for games like this. That's a massive claim after losing the way they did.

The manager said that the responsibility for the failure was his but he repeatedly returned to how lamentable his players were. His players. Six of McInnes' signings started and another two came off the bench.

What has McInnes been doing with his expensively-assembled team. A dozen players have now been signed. How much money has to be spent before the manager starts to look convincing in the role?

The Rangers players who were on the field in the Czech Republic cost about £30m in transfer fees. The wage bill at Ibrox must be astronomical. They've now added the £8.5m winger Kim Min-su and may soon recruit a £9.5m striker in Kevin Kelsy.

The giant wad of cash splurged on all this would choke an elephant.

By contrast, Jablonec's record signing cost around £700,000. Their most recent turnover was £8.5m compared to Rangers' £94m. Their stadium is the size of a shoebox, their support tiny, their European story minimal.

They were the ones who went after the game, though. They didn't have a huge amount going for them in ability terms, but they had edge and character.

Hard work and energy? They trounced Rangers on all of the things that require no talent, just honesty.

McInnes is in a tight spot, not in any danger of losing his job, but with huge amounts of ground to make up with the fans.

He's been around a long time, but the pressure those supporters can exert when things are bad is a challenge for any manager, no matter how long he's been around.

Pittodrie next. A welcome, of sorts, awaits.
authors: Tom English - BBC Scotland's chief sports writer

articles.title: 'This could be some ride' says Southend boss Dyer
articles.summary: Southend United head coach Kieron Dyer says he is embracing the responsibility that management brings after leading his side to three wins in three games.
articles.body:
Southend United head coach Kieron Dyer says he is embracing the responsibility that management brings after leading his side to three wins from his first three games in charge.

The Shrimpers recruited 10 new players over the summer and currently sit top of an embryonic National League table having picked up maximum points.

Dyer, who was appointed as the club's head coach in June, is in his first managerial role after spells coaching at Ipswich Town and Chesterfield.

"The responsibility you have of the team, the club, the office staff. I feel that I have to represent them right," Dyer told BBC Essex.

"It's a big club. When you're taking that on your shoulders it is a mental slog. When you're going to sleep at 9:30 in the evening you know that it's taken its toll.

"But I wouldn't want it any other way. I'm enjoying the responsibility. So let the slog begin."

Amid huge financial problems, Southend have been out of the football league for five years. Their second successive relegation in 2020-21 saw them drop out of the top four divisions for the first time in 101 years.

They came close to a return in June 2025 when the Shrimpers twice led but eventually lost the National League play-off final to Oldham 3-2 after extra-time .

Last season, Southend finished sixth and lost in the play-off semi-finals to Scunthorpe United.

Despite club legend Kevin Maher guiding Southend to FA Trophy success on their return to Wembley in May - the club's first ever domestic trophy - he was dismissed after almost five years in charge following an end of season review conducted by the board.

That opened the door for former Ipswich, Newcastle and England midfielder Dyer, and he admits there were a few self doubts before the start of the season.

"When I was a first-team coach at Ipswich and Chesterfield, I always thought I was a very emotional coach and I used to think that was a weakness," Dyer said.

"And it can be a weakness at times but it can also be a strength. I've just got a level of maturity.

"I didn't know I was ready. It was [Chesterfield boss] Paul Cook who told me I was ready. Two, three years ago I didn't have the maturity to take on the responsibility of looking after players.

"That's just the growth of me as a human being. Let's see where it takes me."

Despite there being another 43 matches still to go in the league, Dyer already has his eyes firmly set on the ultimate goal - promotion.

He added: "When I took the job, I said its the biggest club in the National League. It seems only yesterday Southend were in the Championship.

"I feel this club belongs in the EFL and its my job to get them there. Big club, big fan base. To get over 8,000 fans in the first home match was such a lift for the players.

"If we can get them on board early, this could be some ride."

articles.body:
Manchester City face their first away trip of the 2026-27 Premier League tonight when they take on Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park. Enzo Maresca's side will be looking to build momentum after their late come-from-behind victory at the Etihad Stadium last Sunday.

Crystal Palace will be looking to grab their first points of the season after they were beaten 2-0 by Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium in their opening Premier League fixture of the season last weekend. Crystal Palace are now managed by Pierre Sage. Sage replaced Oliver Glasner as Palace's manager after an impressive spell in charge of RC Lens.

Here is the latest City team news and my predicted Manchester City starting eleven ahead of tonight's match.

Jeremy Doku is the only Manchester City player unavailable for tonight's match due to injury. The Belgian international is currently ruled out due to the calf injury he sustained during the first half of Manchester City's 3-0 FA Community Shield defeat to Arsenal. Elliot Anderson is fit and should start tonight after being substituted against Bournemouth after suffering from cramp. Enzo Maresca also told the media yesterday that Matheus Nunes is continuing to work his way back to full fitness.

Enzo Maresca sprung a surprise last weekend against Bournemouth by starting Marc Guehi in midfield. He could decide to go with that particular move again tonight. Guehi slotted into midfield seamlessly and if asked to step into midfield again, Marc Guehi knows what his manager expects.

New signing Ayyoub Bouaddi is available for selection tonight. Enzo Maresca said yesterday that the Moroccan midfielder is ready to slot straight into the Manchester City matchday squad. If Bouaddi starts, Guehi could move back into defence. However a far more likely scenario is that Bouaddi will start on the bench.

While Matheus Nunes isn't back to full fitness, you do wonder if he could start at right-back for Manchester City tonight. City did look better when Nunes replaced Rico Lewis against Bournemouth and perhaps he could play 60-70 minutes tonight to give City what they need at right-back. Rayan Cherki turned last week's match against Bournemouth and set up both of Manchester City's goals in their 2-1 win. If Cherki is back at full fitness, it would not be a surprise to see him start at Selhurst Park tonight.

articles.body:
Watertown's volleyball team records 3-1 win over Sioux Falls Jefferson

The start of the 2026 season couldn't have went much better for Watertown High School's volleyball team and first-year head coach Havyn Heinz.

The Arrows improved to 2-0 on Thursday, Aug. 27, with a 3-1 (25-20, 25-17, 18-25, 25-18) victory over Sioux Falls Jefferson in Watertown's home opener . On Tuesday, Aug. 25, the Arrows posted a 3-1 (26-28, 25-18, 25-20, 25-20) win at Sioux Falls Roosevelt.

The win over Jefferson likely could mean more since both Watertown and Jefferson received votes in the Class AA preseason poll.

"Jefferson is a very athletic team and they're young," Heinz said. "They're good and you can't overlook them, that's for sure."

Watertown didn't dominate the first two sets but led pretty much from start to finish. Jefferson rebounded in the third set, jumping out to a 6-0 lead and keeping the Arrows at bay. Watertown kicked off the final set with an 8-2 run and put away the Cavaliers.

"In the third set you could tell we were playing tense and just not trusting each other," Heinz said. "At the start of the fourth set, I told them we have to focus on ourselves, have fun and compete. That's the type of volleyball we have to play."

Torrence Tipton smacked 11 kills, Reese Munger eight and Carighan Klatt six to the lead the Arrows. Klatt contributed 11 digs and Munger three solo and two block assits. Andi Olson went 16-17 serving with five aces, Maryn York 17-19 with two aces and Hensley Hogue 18-18. Olson also had 21 digs and Hogue 16. Carighan Klatt smacked 18 kills and Tipton 17 to lead the Arrows against Roosevelt. Kettwig made 50 assists, Olson 21 digs, Hogue 17 digs and Carighan Klatt 11 digs. Munger had two solo blocks and three assists and Kali Ellis and Cambrie Klatt each 2-1.

Jefferson (1-1) received 14 kills from Jadaya Blackburn and nine from Makiah Sharpe. Olivia Wachal recorded 24 assists and Brianna Kindvall 14 digs.

Heinz, a 2020 graduate of Huron High School, is in her first season as a head volleyball coach.

articles.title: Chargers vs. Rams preseason Week 3: 5 takeaways from LA's loss
articles.summary: The Chargers suffered a 20-18 loss to the Rams in the final preseason game. Here is a deeper breakdown of the game.
articles.body:
The Chargers finished the preseason 1-2 after a 20-18 loss to the Rams on Thursday night.

Here's what to take away from the game, which was the final opportunity for players on the roster bubble to prove they deserve a place on the 53-man roster.

Desrosiers was the story of the night, finishing with 9 carries for 118 yards and a 34-yard touchdown on Thursday. It was by far his strongest performance, putting him firmly in the mix for RB4 with Amar Johnson and Jaret Patterson. That title likely does not come with a roster spot - the Chargers have Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell, and Kimani Vidal, plus Alec Ingold at fullback - but Desrosiers might force LA to keep two running backs on the practice squad. Patterson did not play on Thursday. Johnson had 37 yards on 7 carries, all of which came in the second and third quarters.

DJ Uiagalelei outplayed Trey Lance on Thursday, looking more comfortable throwing the ball and moving the offense, albeit against players further down the Rams' depth chart. But Uiagalelei also took three straight sacks, the first of which was nullified by an offsides call, the last of which resulted in a fumble that lost the Chargers the game. That's not the kind of final impression you want to leave in a competition where Lance has played the first half in all three games. It looks more like the Chargers will be monitoring the external quarterback market this weekend and trying to keep Uiagalelei on the practice squad than keeping either of their options as the primary backup to Justin Herbert.

Cameron Dicker appeared to tweak something on the opening kickoff of the game, as punter JK Scott took the remainder of kickoffs on Thursday. Dicker came out for one other play, a 49-yard field goal at the end of the first half that slid wide right. He has now missed a kick in all three weeks of the preseason. The Chargers went for 2 after scoring a touchdown in the second half and had Scott taking practice kicks with Dicker holding late in the game to prepare for a potential game-winner as well. Scott did not have a good day punting the ball, with two kicks of 20 and 33 yards, respectively, among his three punts on the night. His roster spot feels the most tenuous it's ever been despite the Chargers not having another punter on the roster.

Justin Herbert uncorking a deep ball to Quentin Johnston in the first quarter was a welcome reminder of what the Chargers offense could look like once the starters take the helm in Week 1. Not only have fans not seen Herbert launch a ball downfield to an open receiver like that in seemingly forever, but Johnston easily made the catch and walked into the end zone. If the vibes remain high early in the year, that deep shot may be the lasting memory of the catalyst, and for now serves as an appetizer of sorts as Chargers fans continue to get excited about the Mike McDaniel offense.

When the starting unit was mixed in on defense, the run defense looked mighty capable. Linebacker Daiyan Henley knifed through the line to stop Jordan Waters for a loss of 2, forcing the Rams to settle for a field goal after Herbert fumbled a handoff with Omarion Hampton. On the next drive, rookie defensive tackle Nick Barrett and second-year linebacker Marlowe Wax stuffed Waters for no gain inside the 5-yard line. The Rams went for it on fourth and 1, but safety Tony Jefferson came off the edge to wrap Waters around the ankles and force a turnover on downs. It was a healthy showing for the Chargers, who held the Rams to an average of 3.8 yards a carry on the night as a whole.

articles.title: Pitt vs Miami University Prediction: Which Panther Team Will Show Up?
articles.summary: Pitt is good enough to win the ACC, and flaky enough to lose to a Miami University team that might win the MAC. Here's the CFN preview and prediction.
articles.body:
Pitt is a lot of things, but it's certainly not boring. It was good enough to be deep in the hunt for the ACC Championship until the end, and then it lost to East Carolina in the Military Bowl. Yeah, okay, it's a bowl, and several players take off, but the program also dropped the GameAbove Sports Bowl to Toledo the season before. Under head coach Pat Narduzzi, Pitt is a program that could beat Tennessee and Clemson early in 2021, and lose to Western Michigan. It could start 7-0 in 2024 and end up 7-6. And it could have a team good enough to push for the ACC Championship and a College Football Playoff spot, yet still lose to a Miami University team with the makeup to win this without being the slightest bit stunning.

It's all about consistency with Pitt. It has dangerous playmakers on offense, and, as always, its pass rush will be great, but the team has to set a tone for the season with an even effort.

Miami University has to challenge the Pitt secondary. The Panthers have a few new starters, and they'll be under pressure right away.

Pitt has won six straight season openers and 11 of the last 12. Miami has lost 16 of the last 18 openers – the three-game 2020 season was one outlier, and the other win was against Presbyterian in 2015 .

Date: Saturday, September 5, 2026 Game Time: 12:30 pm ET TV: CW Location: Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh, PA – CFN Week 1 Schedule, Predictions

Miami University has the type of team to take the game tempo and grind it down to a dead stop – or, at least, play at its own pace. It might not have a whole lot of returning firepower, and it'll be in big trouble if it has to get into any sort of firefight, but it'll keep the chains moving, the ground game will be effective behind a terrific offensive line, and the defense, with its fabulous pass rush, can take care of the rest. – Miami University 2026 Preview

Score fast, make Miami bust out of its shell, and then turn the pass rush loose. As good as the RedHawks are and will be, they're replacing almost all of the key skill parts. They brought in plenty of options through the portal, but there aren't enough high-end starters to worry about an explosion. – Pitt 2026 Preview

Pitt vs Miami University Prediction, Betting Lines

Pitt will get star quarterback Mason Heintschel going early, but this year's team has the running game with Ja'Kyrian Turner and Western Kentucky's La'Vell Wright to take over at times. Miami University's new offensive coordinator Gus Ragland will try to open things up a bit more and get the passing game going, but it'll be the defense that will keep this close. The Drake football team lost to South Dakota Mines 38-35 on Aug. 27 at Drake Stadium. The Bulldogs scored three touchdowns in the fourth quarter but came up short in their season opener.

"I'm searching for words right now," Drake's first-year coach Matt Walker said. "That was not the way any of us wanted to start. So much credit to (South Dakota Mines), but we made mistakes that you just cannot have."

The two teams totaled nearly 1,100 yards of offense, with Drake racking up 559. Bulldogs quarterback Riley Warzynski passed for a school-record 535 yards, outdoing the previous mark of 455 set by Mike Grejbowski in 1970.

Drake's Willis Nofsinger finished with 168 receiving yards. Hank Foley added 146.

Linebacker J.R. Flood led Drake with a career-best 18 tackles.

Drake's next game is at Montana on Sept. 5.

Drake sports information contributed to this report .

articles.title: Grading Ty Simpson's performance vs. Chargers
articles.summary: Ty Simpson ended the preseason on a high note with another outstanding performance for the Rams.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams gave Stetson Bennett the night off in Thursday's preseason finale , starting Ty Simpson in his place. It was Simpson's first start of the preseason, allowing the rookie to feel what it's like to take the first snaps of a game.

Knowing he's probably the No. 3 quarterback behind Matthew Stafford and Bennett, this was likely Simpson's last game until next August. Things would have to go terribly sideways for the Rams in order for Simpson to play meaningful snaps, so the team hopes he'll be on the shelf for all of 2026.

He picked up where he left off in the first two preseason games, looking sharp and confident once again on Thursday night. The Rams moved the pocket with some roll-outs and play-action fakes, getting Simpson into a rhythm. But there were also enough straight drop-backs to give him some pro-style looks.

He did a great job spreading the ball around, hitting six different receivers on the first three drives. He started the game a near-perfect 11-for-12 passing, and the one incompletion was a dropped pass by Tyler Scott on a ball that was slightly high. The Rams' third possession was their best one of the first quarter, going 79 yards in 17 plays, but they did come up empty after getting stuffed on four straight running plays from inside the 5.

Nate Scheelhaase took the ball out of Simpson's hands and ran it four times in a row with Dean Connors and Jordan Waters, much to the frustration of fans.

Simpson came out firing on the next drive and made his best throw of the preseason for a touchdown. He faced quick pressure from the Chargers, rolled out to his left and threw a dime to Brennan Presley on the run in the end zone. It showed off his athleticism, arm strength and accuracy off-platform, which are all important traits for a quarterback.

Throughout the night, Simpson was comfortable in the pocket, and even when he was pressured, he didn't panic. He didn't take off sooner than he should have, nor did he stand there oblivious to the defenders around him.

For a rookie, it was impressive to see him stand tall in the pocket and make throws when a lot of other guys would've quickly tucked the ball and run.

On his final two drives, there were a few more inaccuracies than earlier in the game, completing seven of his final 11 passes. He tried to force a throw to CJ Daniels in the corner of the end zone on third down in the red zone, despite the receiver being double-covered. On the next play, Alex Bachman was his target on a fade route, but Simpson threw it out of bounds and didn't give his receiver a chance.

He then had a coaching lesson with Sean McVay on the sideline afterwards, with the coach giving him a few tips.

Simpson's night (essentially) ended at halftime. He was replaced by Matthew Caldwell in the third quarter, finishing the night with another quality stat line: 18-for-23, 119 yards and one touchdown with no turnovers. His passer rating was 102.7, and he rushed for 11 yards on two carries. Simpson did have to re-enter the game late in the fourth quarter after Caldwell was shaken up on a run play, but didn't throw a pass.

He didn't take any real deep shots or push the ball downfield much, but for the third straight week, he took what the defense gave him. He checked it down when he couldn't find anyone open and allowed his receivers to pick up yards after the catch.

If this is the last time we see Simpson until next preseason, he ended his first summer on a high note with a solid performance.

articles.title: ‘Burgers falls in Greensboro
articles.summary: GREENSBORO, N.C. — After a blowout win on Wednesday night, Hub City could not follow up against Greensboro on Thursday. The Grasshoppers (75-48, 34-23) attac...
articles.body:
GREENSBORO, N.C. — After a blowout win on Wednesday night, Hub City could not follow up against Greensboro on Thursday. The Grasshoppers (75-48, 34-23) attacked the Spartanburgers (56-67, 22-35) early en route to an 11-4 win.

Greensboro turned to lefty Reinold Navarro on the mound against Hub City's Jormy Nivar , making his High-A debut. Both starters faced the minimum in the first before finding trouble in the second.

Maxton Martin reached to kick off the frame on a dropped third strike. Quincy Scott immediately capitalized with a two-run homer the opposite way. Navarro worked around two walks later in the inning to limit the damage to two. The Grasshoppers immediately tied the game again on back-to-back home runs from Jared Jones and Tony Blanco Jr. to lead off the bottom of the second. Blanco was batting out of order when he slugged the second home run, but it came without appeal from the Spartanburgers. Jhonny Severino then struck out, a spot later than assigned.

After a scoreless top of the third, Greensboro took its first lead. A single and hit batter started the inning. After two outs from Nivar (L, 0-1), Jones walked to load the bases. Severino came to the plate in the correct order and lined in two runs with a single to center field. Blanco followed suit with an RBI single to make it 5-2 Grasshoppers. Anthony Susac relieved Nivar and provided the final out of the third.

Hub City forced Greensboro to its 'pen with the bases full and one out in the fourth. Cesar Aquino entered and rolled a fielder's choice off the bat of Evan Morrison to bring in a run. Gleider Figuereo added another tally with an RBI single to make it 5-4.

Greensboro immediately upped the lead in the fourth off Susac. The righty walked the bases loaded to start the inning. Edward Florentino doubled to right to drive in two runs. An out later, Jones grounded a two-run single back up the middle. The Grasshoppers led 9-4.

Facing Aquino in the fifth, the 'Burgers had a chance to respond. Paxton Kling singled and a pair of walks loaded the bases. Greensboro manager Jose Mosquera went back to his bullpen, and lefty Victor Cabreja (W, 8-4) ended the inning with a strikeout and a flyout. Hub City was held scoreless for the rest of the game.

Kai Wynyard threw 2 2/3 perfect innings from the fourth through sixth. The Grasshoppers tacked on two more runs in the late stages against Cole Roland . Jones roped a second solo homer in the seventh. Dylan Palmer tripled Shalin Polanco home in the eighth.

On Friday, first pitch between Hub City and Greensboro is scheduled for 6:30 p.m. ET. The Spartanburgers send left-hander Ben DeTaeye (2-0, 8.31 ERA) to the mound, and the Grasshoppers counter with southpaw Jacob Bimbi (5-3, 2.97 ERA).

articles.title: HS Standouts: Calvin McCoy Greer High School
articles.summary: GREER, S.C. - Greer High School senior running back Calvin McCoy has built his game around a simple motto Head Football Coach Will Young instills in his play...
articles.body:
GREER, S.C. - Greer High School senior running back Calvin McCoy has built his game around a simple motto Head Football Coach Will Young shares with his players: "Earned, not given."

He first stepped onto a football field to help manage anger issues. At the time, he was a bigger kid playing tackle. Years later, he's transformed into one of the Upstate's most productive running backs, helping lead the Yellow Jackets with the same philosophy that's printed across the program.

"It's on our shirts that we have... 'Earned, not given,'" said McCoy. "You got to work for everything. Everything is not going to be a handout."

The motto reflects McCoy's path through the program. After beginning his career on the offensive line, McCoy eventually moved into the backfield when Greer needed someone to step up.

"I actually played tackle. I was a little bit bigger," said McCoy. "When our players went down, I really just had to step up to the next man."

The opportunity helped him realize something about himself.

"I learned I can do anything I put my mind to," said McCoy.

The results have shown up as he became a monster on the field.

In Greer's 45-31 season-opening victory over Woodmont, McCoy carried the ball 28 times for 207 yards and three touchdowns. He also sealed the win with an interception on defense. The performance came after a breakout junior season in which he rushed for more than 1,300 yards and 13 touchdowns after returning from a concussion suffered during his sophomore year.

Much of his hard work happens when no ones watching.

"I work out a lot, so not a lot of people see that. During the offseason, I was working out like five days a week," said McCoy.

The offseason commitment was fueled by his desire to build on last year's success.

"Honestly, just building on what I built on last year," said McCoy. "That was a big thing because my sophomore year I went down with a concussion and coming back my junior year, that was a big season."

Greer head coach Will Young has witnessed that development firsthand. Now in his 22nd season leading the Yellow Jackets, Young said a noticeable change occurred about a year and a half ago.

"Calvin just approaches life in a different way," said Young. "We saw a flip switch about a year and a half ago, and just every aspect of his life has changed in the weight room, in the classroom and how he functions on the practice field."

Young believes the growth extends beyond football.

"Everybody sees Friday-night stuff and don't realize all the things that go in behind it," Young said.

The longtime coach described McCoy as one of the most mature players on the roster and said he has emerged as a stronger voice within the program.

"He's definitely been one of our more vocal leaders out here, which is probably something that's a little out of his comfort zone, but he's figured out how to do it," Young said.

McCoy said becoming more confident and independent has been one of his goals entering his senior season.

"Being more me and more independent," said McCoy. "That's a big skill."

While football has helped shape him as a player, Greer has helped shape him as a person. McCoy grew up just across the street from Dooley Field where he now stars on Friday nights, and said the town's sports culture is unlike anywhere else.

"Honestly, the community is great," said McCoy. "The clock, that's like a Greer staple out here."

He pointed to rivalries with Byrnes and Riverside as examples of what makes the area special.

"Football means everything because it's really all I got for real," said McCoy.

Even with those rivalries, McCoy views the community as one extended family.

As the season progresses, college coaches are beginning to take notice. McCoy confirmed he has received one college offer, though he is keeping the school's identity private while evaluating his options.

When the time comes to choose a program, he already knows what he wants.

"Honestly, the tradition," said McCoy. "I'm big on tradition and brotherhood."

He also values the connections teammates build away from the field, and feels grateful after receiving his first offer.

"It was honestly surreal because I manifested it and it finally came," said McCoy. "It came in the offseason a couple of months ago."

Young believes more opportunities could be on the horizon.

"He's definitely a college-caliber guy," said Young. "I think somebody is going to take a shot on him. With his grades now, he's a qualifier. Make some money, come get him."

For McCoy, however, the focus remains the same. Whether it's carrying the football, leading younger teammates, or navigating the recruiting process, his approach is rooted in the message he's embraced since arriving at Greer.
